turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Hey you! Finally got a free evening to chat. How's the week been?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Long but fine. Work has been hectic at Mossgate Studio, we've got a big deadline coming up, but I survived.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Ha, survived is the key word. Did you at least get outside at all this weekend?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Yes! I finally did that ridge trail you kept recommending. The first half is brutal uphill but the view at the top made up for it.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Told you! Did you do the loop back through the pine section? That part is my favorite.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: I did, and my knees were not thrilled by the end. I basically hobbled to the car.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Worth it though. Oh, did you hear Tove and Anders finally set a date for the wedding?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: I did, it's on a farm somewhere out in the countryside, right? I'm excited, I just have no idea what to wear.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Same. I'm told it's semi-formal, which means nothing to me. I'll probably just panic-buy a jacket the week before.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Classic you. Speaking of panic, I tried making a risotto last night and it turned into something closer to glue.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Oh no. Did you add all the stock at once? That's the usual crime.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Absolutely guilty. I got distracted by my phone and by the time I looked up it was a solid brick of rice. We ended up eating toast.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Toast dinner is underrated, honestly. I do it at least once a week and don't regret it.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Fair. Oh, I also picked up a new plant on the way home yesterday, the pothos. It's already trailing off my bookshelf like it owns the place.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Nice, those are hard to kill, which is perfect for you. Send me a picture once it's settled in.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Will do. Alright, I should go figure out dinner that isn't toast. Talk in a couple of weeks?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Sounds good. Good luck with the deadline, and with not burning anything!

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Hey you! Finally got a quiet evening, so I'm on the sofa with tea and nothing planned. How's your week been?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Pretty slow, which I'm not complaining about. I've been daydreaming about a holiday though, maybe somewhere with mountains and no phone signal.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Ooh yes. I keep going back and forth between a lazy beach week and a proper hiking trip. Probably I'd get bored on the beach by day three.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Same. Maybe a road trip would be the compromise, a bit of coast, a bit of hills, and no fixed plan.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Road trip sounds right. Funny enough I only have a small boot to work with, I drive a Honda Jazz, so we'd have to pack light.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Packing light is a good rule anyway. Did you watch anything good lately? I finally saw that old sci-fi film everyone raves about.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Wait, I need to fix something I just said. I don't drive a Honda Jazz, that was a slip on my part, it's a Volvo V60. Much bigger boot, so maybe packing light isn't a rule after all.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Ha, that's a pretty big slip, those are very different cars. Fine, you're officially in charge of luggage on the road trip then.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Deal. Okay, tell me about the film, was it worth the hype?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Mostly yes. The first hour is slow but the ending stuck with me for days, and the soundtrack is unreal. I'd watch it again just for that.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Adding it to my list. I've been in a rut with films, I keep rewatching the same comfort ones.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Nothing wrong with comfort films. I do the same with cooking, actually, and last weekend that went badly. I tried a creamy pasta bake and the sauce split into this greasy mess.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Oh no. Did you add the cheese when it was too hot? That's what usually does it to me.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Probably, I was impatient and just dumped it all in. We ended up eating toast with the rescued noodles on the side.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Honestly that sounds like a decent dinner. Next time take the pan off the heat first and stir the cheese in slowly.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Noted, I'll try again this weekend. Talk in a couple of weeks? I want to hear where the road trip planning goes.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Definitely. I'll start collecting ideas. Sleep well!

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Hey you! Survived the weekend? I spent most of mine catching up on sleep, which feels very grown up and very sad.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Ha, same energy here. I mostly lay on the sofa and listened to that podcast I told you about, the one with the two guys who investigate old local mysteries.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Oh the one about the missing lighthouse keeper? I started it on Friday, I'm only two episodes in but I'm hooked.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Yes that's the one! Don't skip ahead, episode five has a twist I did not see coming.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: No spoilers, I'm warning you. Anyway, big news on my end, I finally switched jobs, I'm at Halvorsen Freight now and so far the people seem really decent.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Wait, congrats! That's great, I want the full story next time. Is the commute any better at least?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Marginally. I'll tell you everything soon, but right now my brain is full of wedding logistics for Tove and Anders.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Right, the wedding! Have you figured out what you're wearing? I'm still staring at a suit that I think shrank in the closet.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Suits don't shrink, Isak, you just ate well over winter. I'm wearing the green dress, finally found shoes that don't destroy my feet.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Fair, fair. I hear they've booked a band instead of a DJ, so there's going to be actual dancing and no hiding.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Terrifying. Also, unrelated, I bought a new plant on Saturday, the fiddle-leaf fig, and it's already dropping one leaf out of spite.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Those things are divas, I've heard. Mine would be dead in a week, I can barely keep a basil plant going.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: I'm giving it the brightest corner and talking to it nicely. Meanwhile the neighbour upstairs decided 11pm was a good time to move furniture last night.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Ugh, the noisy neighbour saga continues. Did you knock on the door or just stew silently like a normal person?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Stewed silently, obviously. My sister Ingrid says I should leave a polite note, but I'm more of a passive-aggressive ceiling-thumping type.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Honestly the note is the classier move. Try it, and if that fails, we escalate to thumping together.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Deal. Okay, I need to go make dinner, talk in a couple of weeks? And report back on episode five.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Hey you. Sorry I went quiet, the last couple of weeks have been a blur.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: No worries, I've been bad at replying too. How's everything otherwise?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Mostly fine except the neighbour upstairs. He started practising drums at ten at night. Drums! Who does that?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Oh no. Have you said anything to him yet or are you still in the passive-aggressive sigh phase?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Sigh phase. I left a very polite note and he responded by playing quieter for exactly one evening.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Classic. Did you get the wedding invitation, by the way? Dagny's, I mean.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Yes! It came last week. I'm so happy for them, though I'm already nervous about the dinner, because I'm allergic to shellfish and weddings love a seafood starter.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Good point, you should flag that on the RSVP. They're pretty organised, they'll sort you out something.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: That's what I figured. I'll tick the box and hope for the best. Are you going to give a speech or just heckle?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Heckle, obviously. Although I did get asked to say a few words at the rehearsal thing, so I need to come up with something not embarrassing.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Ha, good luck with that. Tell the story about the broken tent at the festival.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: That's the embarrassing one! But yeah, it might work if I keep it short.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Anyway, I started a new podcast on my commute that you'd probably like. It's two historians arguing about famous bridges, weirdly gripping.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Bridges? That sounds oddly perfect. Send me the name and I'll give it a go on my run tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Will do, I'll text it over in a sec. Fair warning, the hosts bicker a lot.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Bickering is a feature, not a bug. Talk soon, and good luck with the drummer.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Hey you! Survived the long weekend? I basically did nothing, which was glorious.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Same, mostly. I had a dentist appointment this morning, so the weekend's good mood has officially worn off.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Ugh, sorry. Is that the same one you've been going to for ages?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Yep, still Dr. Okafor. She's great, I just hate the scraping sound.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Fair. Anyway, I finally watched that slow Icelandic film everyone was raving about. Two hours of a man staring at sheep, and somehow I loved it.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Ha, that sounds exactly like something you'd love. Was it the one with the long shots of the highlands?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: That's the one. The landscape alone carries it, honestly. It made me want to go outside and walk for a week.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Funny you say that, I did the ridge trail on Saturday, the one with the stone steps at the start. The views from the top were unreal, and almost nobody was there.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Jealous. My knees are still complaining about the last time I tried steps like that. Was it muddy?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Only the first bit, then it dries out. Bring proper boots and you'll be fine.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Noted. Should I be watching anything this week? I need something for the evenings.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: I've been working through a miniseries on Lumen, since I subscribe there anyway. It's short and moody, very much your taste.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: I might borrow a free trial and check it out. Have you been listening to anything good lately?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Yes! A podcast about forgotten inventions. Each episode is about some doomed gadget from a hundred years ago, and it's weirdly addictive.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Oh that sounds fun, I'll queue it up for the commute tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Do it. Then we can compare favourite doomed gadgets next time.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Hey you! Survived the week? I finally watched that old noir film everyone keeps going on about last night.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Hey! Mostly survived, yes. Oh nice, which one? Was it as moody as people say?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Extremely moody. Lots of rain, lots of cigarettes, a detective who never smiles once. I loved it, though the ending made no sense to me.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Haha, that's the genre, the ending is never supposed to make sense. I've been meaning to watch something like that, I need a proper cozy night in.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Do it. Speaking of cozy, how's the flat looking these days? Last time you were saying it felt a bit empty.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Better, actually. I picked up the peace lily from a little market stall on Saturday, and it already makes the corner by the window feel less bare.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Nice, those look good even when you ignore them a bit. Did it go in the spot where your old plant was?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Yes, exactly that spot. The fiddle-leaf fig is gone, it dropped leaf after leaf for weeks and I finally had to admit defeat.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Ah, sorry. Fair enough though, you gave it a good run. Anyway, I'm trying to plan some kind of holiday for later this year and I have no ideas at all.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Ooh. Are you thinking beach, or more wandering around somewhere with good food and old streets?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Honestly the second one. Somewhere I can walk all day, sit in cafes, and not think about anything. Maybe a train trip instead of flying.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Train trips are the best, you actually get to watch the country change. I'd go for that over an airport any day.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Agreed. I'd just like to sleep properly first. My neighbour upstairs has started dragging furniture around at midnight, I swear.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Oh no, the classic. Have you said anything, or are you doing the passive-aggressive broom-on-the-ceiling thing?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Broom stage, sadly. I might leave a polite note first, but it's hard to stay polite at one in the morning.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Write the note when you're well rested, it'll come out nicer. Let me know how it goes!

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Hey you. Finally got round to watching that Icelandic film you recommended last time. I think I have to sit with it a few days before I know what I thought.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Ha, that's the right reaction honestly. Which part got you, the long silent stretches or the ending?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: The silences, mostly. Every time I thought someone would finally say something, the camera just stayed on the landscape. Weirdly hypnotic though.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Right? I watched it half asleep the first time and it still worked on me. Oh, before I forget, book club is at Pilcrow Books again this month, same back-room table as usual.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Good, I like that room. I'll bring back the book I borrowed too, I'm only about two thirds through but I'll live.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Nobody's going to check, we mostly just talk about everything except the book anyway.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: True. Anyway, I've been daydreaming about a summer holiday. Somewhere with a coastline and no real plan, just wandering.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: That sounds lovely. I'd be tempted by somewhere green and a bit remote, a place where you can get lost in the hills for a few days.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Now you're talking. Speaking of hills, I did that ridge trail on Sunday, the one with the stone shelter at the top.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Oh nice, how was it? I've heard the last climb is brutal but the view makes up for it.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Brutal is fair. My knees complained the whole way down. But the view was ridiculous, you could see for miles, and it was almost empty because everyone sensibly stayed home.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: I need to do that one soon. Oh, small news, I picked up a new plant this week, the monstera. It's already taking over the corner by the window.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Those things are dramatic in the best way. Does it have the split leaves yet or is it still in the baby phase?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Baby phase, but I'm optimistic. I keep checking it like it's going to grow overnight.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Send me a photo when it does. And let's pick a weekend for that trail, I'll even carry the snacks.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Deal. Snacks carrier is the best job. Talk soon!

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Hey you. Survive the week? You mentioned last time your upstairs situation was getting rough.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Barely. The neighbour was running some kind of power tool at eleven last night. On a Monday. I stood there in my socks glaring at the ceiling like that would help.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Classic. Did you go up and say something?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: I left a very polite note on their door instead. Passive aggression with a smiley face. We'll see if it works.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Bold strategy. Smiley faces are basically a threat.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Exactly the vibe I was going for. Oh, unrelated, I finally cancelled the Lumen subscription. I kept paying for it and barely opened it.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Ha, good for you. I have like three of those I keep meaning to kill off. Did you at least watch anything decent lately?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: I saw an old film on a friend's couch, a slow Scandinavian thing about two brothers and a broken-down ferry. Sounds dull, but I couldn't look away.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: That actually sounds like my kind of thing. Was it sad or just quietly bleak?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Quietly bleak with moments of surprisingly dry humour. The ending left me staring at the credits for a while.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Okay, adding it to my list. I've mostly been outside instead. Did the ridge trail on Saturday, the one with the long stone staircase near the start.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Oh nice, how was it? I've heard the staircase kills your legs.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: It does, but the view at the top makes up for it. You can see right across the valley, and there was hardly anyone there.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Okay, now I want to go. Is it doable in a day without being a total slog?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Totally. Start early, bring more water than you think you need, and it's easy. Want to try it together sometime?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Yes, let's. Pick a weekend that isn't raining and I'm in. I'll even promise not to complain about the staircase.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Hey you! Finally sitting down with a coffee, how's your week been?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Pretty good, busy but fine. I've been daydreaming about a holiday though, anywhere that isn't my desk.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Ha, same. I keep flicking between a beach week and one of those slow train trips through the mountains.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Train trip sounds dreamy. I'd probably fall asleep with my face against the window, but happily.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Oh, random life update: I switched dentists recently and I'm with Dr. Abernathy now. Had my first check-up and it was oddly painless.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Painless is the dream with dentists. Glad it went well!

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Right? Also I finally sorted out my phone situation and I'm paying $44 a month now, which feels like a win.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Nice, any saving is a good saving. I should really look at mine, I haven't in ages.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Do it, it only takes an evening. Anyway, are you going to Tove's wedding? I still can't believe she's actually tying the knot.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Wouldn't miss it. I heard it's an outdoor ceremony, so I'm hoping the weather behaves.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Fingers crossed. This weekend looks lovely at least, sunny all day Saturday apparently.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Perfect. I'm thinking a long walk and then lying in the grass doing nothing. Any plans on your end?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Tidying the flat mostly, since I've got a bit more space on the windowsill now that the monstera is gone. It didn't make it in the end.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Aw, sorry to hear that. Well, at least you get a sunnier windowsill out of it.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: True! Okay, I'll let you get on with your day. Talk in a couple of weeks?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Definitely. Enjoy the sunshine and say hi to the weekend for me!

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Hey, you alive? Feels like forever since we last talked.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Barely! It's been a week of heat and bad sleep. How are you doing?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Pretty good. I finally did that ridge trail I kept going on about, the one with the long gravel climb at the start.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Oh nice, how was it? Did the view actually make up for the climb?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Totally. Clear day, hardly anyone up there, and I sat at the top eating a very sad sandwich and felt great.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Ha, the sad sandwich is part of the ritual. I should get out more like that. I mostly just drag myself to the gym these days, I've got a membership at the Ironbridge gym and I'm weirdly loyal to it.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Weirdly loyal is the good kind. Better than paying for something and never going.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: True. Anyway, the reason I'm sleeping badly is my upstairs neighbour. Somebody there drags furniture around at midnight.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Midnight furniture rearranging is a crime. Have you said anything to them?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Not yet. I keep hoping it'll stop on its own, but I think I'm going to have to leave a polite note.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Polite note first, then escalate to passive aggressive baking. Works every time.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Ha, I'll keep that in my back pocket. Okay, change of subject, I need something to look forward to. Have you thought about a holiday this year?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: A bit. I'm leaning toward somewhere cooler, maybe mountains and lakes, nothing too busy.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: That sounds perfect. I'd want a mix, a few lazy days and then one proper adventure so I don't feel like I wasted it.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Same. Lazy days with one adventure sprinkled in is the ideal ratio.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Right? Let's compare ideas next time we chat. I'll do some actual research this week.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Deal. Go get some sleep, and good luck with the furniture person.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Hey you! Finally sitting down with a coffee after a very long Monday. How's your week starting?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Slow and pleasant, honestly. I've been listening to this podcast about lost shipwrecks on my walks, and I'm weirdly hooked.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Ha, that sounds right up your street. Is it one of those with dramatic music and a hushed narrator?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Exactly that. The narrator whispers like he's afraid of waking the ship up.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Work news, by the way, I don't think I told you properly. I'm at Tallow & Pine now, and so far it feels like a much better fit.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Oh nice, that's good to hear! You sounded pretty ready for a change.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: I was. Everyone's been welcoming, and nobody has scheduled a meeting that could have been an email yet.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Give it a month. Anyway, are we still on for book club this week? I'm planning to head to Marginalia straight after work, it's been our spot all along.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: I'll try, depends how the week shapes up. I watched a film last night, though, an old black and white thing my neighbour recommended.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Oh? Was it any good, or one of those where you stay loyal out of politeness?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Properly good, actually. Slow, but the ending stuck with me for hours afterwards.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Those are the best kind. I need something like that, I've been rewatching comfort shows far too much lately.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Nothing wrong with comfort shows. Oh, and I picked up a new plant at the weekend, the jade plant. It's sitting on my windowsill looking smug.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Smug is the right word for jade plants. Let's hope it survives your enthusiasm.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Rude, but fair. Have you thought about any holiday plans? I'm craving somewhere with water and no schedule.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Same. Somewhere coastal and quiet, with a book and nothing to be on time for. I'd happily do that for a week.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: That's the dream. Let's compare notes next time and maybe actually commit to something.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Okay, I need to tell you about the disaster I made last night. I tried a new braised chicken recipe and somehow ended up with something closer to chicken soup with a crust on top.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Ha, how does that even happen? Did you forget to put the lid on or something?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: I think I did the opposite. The recipe said to cover it for the whole hour and I'm pretty sure it needed the lid off for the last twenty minutes. Lesson learned, I guess.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: I once made a risotto that came out like wallpaper paste. Cooking is basically just a series of small humiliations.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Wallpaper paste, that's vivid. At least mine was edible, just very sad looking. I ate it standing at the counter like it was a secret.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Honestly the best way to eat a failed dinner. Anyway, have you listened to anything good lately? I've been stuck on a podcast about abandoned railway lines and I can't stop.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: That sounds weirdly right up my alley. I've been working through one about the history of everyday objects, like the zipper and the paperclip. Sounds dull, it's actually really funny.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Okay, now I'm adding that to my list. The railway one has this host who gets way too emotional about old signal boxes, which is why I love it.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Emotional about signal boxes is the energy I want in a podcast host. Do you listen while you walk, or just at home?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Mostly while I'm out walking, actually. I finally did that ridge trail I kept talking about last weekend, the one with the long climb at the start.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Oh nice, how was it? I remember you saying the first stretch was supposed to be brutal.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Brutal but worth it. The view from the top was ridiculous, you could see all the way across the valley, and there was hardly anyone else up there.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Now I'm jealous. I haven't been properly hiking in ages, I keep saying I'll go and then the weekend disappears.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: You should come next time, it's not too steep once you're past the first bit. I'll even bring snacks so you don't have to cook anything.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Deal, as long as the snacks aren't another one of your experimental trail mixes. The last one had something in it I still can't identify.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: That was dried pear, it's a classic! Fine, I'll keep it simple. Let's pick a weekend soon.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Hey Isak! Finally sitting down for a proper chat. How's your week been?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Pretty decent, just slow. I've been listening to that podcast about lost expeditions on my walks, it's weirdly gripping.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Oh nice, is that the one with the two hosts who keep arguing about maps? I started it last week and got hooked on the second episode.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Yes, that one! The arguing is half the charm. What's new with you, anything happening?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Actually yes, big news on the work front. I switched jobs and I'm at Corvid Analytics now, started a couple of weeks ago.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Congrats, that's a big move! How are the first weeks treating you?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Good so far, people are friendly. Also I finally changed dentists, I'm seeing Dr. Yoon now and the office is so much calmer than my old one.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: A calm dentist is a rare find, hang onto that. Are you settled in otherwise?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Mostly, yes. I'm in Graz and still figuring out which bakery is my favourite.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Ha, a worthy quest. Any plans for the weekend, or is the weather going to decide for you?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Oops, correction, I typed the wrong city a second ago. It's Dunedin, not Graz, my brain is clearly still on a different track today.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Ha, no worries, that happens. Anyway, the forecast here says rain on Saturday and sun on Sunday, so I'm planning a long walk on Sunday.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Same pattern here, grey Saturday, then it clears up. I might go for a coastal walk and finish the podcast, and I'm paying $38 a month for my phone now so at least I can stream it without worrying.

turns.text: Perfect plan. Meanwhile my upstairs neighbour has started moving furniture around at eleven at night, I swear he rearranges his flat daily.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Oh no, that's the worst. Have you tried leaving a friendly note? Sometimes people honestly have no idea how much it carries.

turns.speaker: Isak

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Okay, I finally have news on the wedding front. Did you get the invite from Tobias and Lena too?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Yes! It landed on my doormat on Saturday, with a little pressed flower tucked inside. Very fancy.

turns.text: Ha, ours had one too. I'm already stressing about what to wear, since they said 'garden formal', whatever that means.

turns.text: I think it means don't wear heels you'll sink into the lawn with. I'm planning on a linen jacket and hoping for the best.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Smart. Honestly I'm more excited about the day after, when everyone's hungover and we all end up at some greasy café.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: That's the real highlight of any wedding. Speaking of food, I tried making a risotto last night and it was a disaster.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Oh no, what happened? Risotto is one of those things that looks easy and then isn't.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: I got distracted answering a message and the bottom scorched, then I panicked and added way too much stock. It ended up somewhere between soup and porridge.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Soup-porridge, the forbidden dish. Did you eat it anyway?

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: I did, with a lot of cheese on top. Cheese covers a multitude of sins.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Truly. Anyway, I've been daydreaming about a trip lately, maybe somewhere with a coast and not much to do except wander around.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: That sounds perfect. I keep thinking about going somewhere quiet in the off-season, when the crowds have gone home.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Yes, exactly that. Cold sea air, a big jumper, long lunches. I'd take that over a beach any day.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: We should actually plan something instead of just talking about it for another year.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Deal. Let's pick a rough direction after the wedding, once the outfit crisis is over.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Sounds good. And I'll practise the risotto again so I can redeem myself.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Okay, I have to tell you about the film I watched last night. It was supposed to be a quiet little drama and it turned into a two-hour stare at a man fixing a boat.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Ha, I think I know the one. Was the boat a metaphor or just a boat?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Honestly I couldn't tell. Someone behind me in the cinema sighed so loudly at the end that I almost clapped.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Brutal. I watched something much dumber on Friday, a heist thing where everyone wears sunglasses indoors. Loved every minute.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Sometimes that's exactly what you need. Did you get the invite for Tomas and Elin's wedding, by the way?

turns.text: Yes! Finally someone in our circle is doing it properly, with a long weekend and everything. I'm already worried about the speeches.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Tomas said he's writing his own vows and refuses to show anyone. That's either going to be beautiful or a disaster.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Knowing him, both at once. I'll bring tissues and a straight face.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Smart. Oh, I tried making that braised cabbage recipe you sent me and it went sideways.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Oh no, what happened? That one is nearly impossible to ruin.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: I turned the heat up to speed it along and ended up with something between charcoal and soup. The whole flat smelled like a campfire for a day.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Okay, that's impressive, I'll give you that. The trick is patience, it really does want low and slow.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Lesson learned. I ordered a pizza and called it a night.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Honestly the correct decision. I once set off the smoke alarm making toast, so I'm not judging.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Toast is a bold way to go out. Let's talk in two weeks, and send me a better recipe by then, one with fewer ways to fail.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Deal. I'll find you something foolproof, or at least fool-resistant.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Hey you! Finally got a quiet evening, so I thought I'd catch up properly. How's your week been?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Pretty calm, honestly. I watched a film on Tuesday night that I'd been meaning to see for ages, that slow Norwegian one about the lighthouse keeper.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Oh, the one with the long silent stretches? I tried watching that and fell asleep twenty minutes in. Was it worth sticking with?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Ha, yes, it's very much a fall-asleep film at the start. But the ending got me. The last half hour is gorgeous, all fog and gulls and this one huge storm scene.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Okay, I'll give it another go then. Maybe not right before bed this time.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Definitely not. Afternoon with a big mug of tea is the way to do it.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Noted. Hey, did you ever do that ridge trail you were talking about? The one with the stone hut at the top?

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Not yet! I keep eyeing it but every time I plan it, the forecast turns grim. I read that the last stretch gets really slippery when it's wet.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Yeah, I did it years ago and the final scramble is no joke in the rain. Worth it for the view though, you can see all the way down the valley on a clear day.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: That's exactly the view I want. Speaking of which, do you know what the weather's doing this weekend? I haven't looked yet.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: I glanced earlier and it looked decent. Cold and bright on Saturday, then clouds rolling in on Sunday with maybe some drizzle.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Cold and bright is perfect hiking weather. Saturday morning might finally be the day for that ridge.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Do it! Start early, take a flask, and bring gloves because the wind up top is brutal this time of year.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Good tip, I'd have forgotten the gloves for sure. I'll send you a photo from the hut if I make it.

turns.speaker: Isak
turns.text: Please do. And I'll report back on whether I survive the lighthouse film in the afternoon.

turns.speaker: Maren
turns.text: Deal. Talk in a couple of weeks, and good luck staying awake!

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Happy new year, Corwin! Did you get any real time off, or were you checking Slack the whole break?

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Happy new year! I tried to stay away and mostly managed. Only peeked twice, which for me is basically a vacation.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Respect. I came back to find the office coffee machine making a horrible grinding noise. Sounds like a blender full of gravel.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Oh no, I heard about that. Somebody taped a sign on it that just says 'be gentle.' I don't think that's a maintenance plan.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Ha, no. I've started going to the little cafe downstairs instead. It's a bit pricey but at least it doesn't scream at me.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Fair. I'll probably join you if it's not fixed by Wednesday.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Deal. On a less fun note, I spent part of this morning chasing a flaky test. It passes, it fails, it passes again, no changes in between.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Ugh, the worst kind. Is it a timing thing, you think?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Probably something like that. I'll poke at it more tomorrow, but I'm not hopeful it's a quick fix.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Well, don't sink the whole week into it. If it's truly random, maybe we quarantine it and note it down so it doesn't get forgotten.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: That's reasonable. Noting things down is a whole other problem though. Our documentation is in rough shape.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Don't remind me. Half the setup guides still describe how things worked a long time ago. I keep meaning to block out time for it.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Same. I rewrote one page before the holidays and it felt great, like cleaning out a closet. Then I looked at how many other pages there are and felt less great.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Maybe we pick one page each sprint and just chip away. Small and steady beats a big heroic cleanup that never happens.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: I like that. Low pressure, and we actually might stick to it.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Great, I'll add it to the agenda for our next planning meeting. Talk in a couple of weeks, and good luck with that test!

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Hey Corwin, finally got my new laptop set up yesterday. The old one was wheezing every time I opened more than three browser tabs.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Ha, about time. How is it? Fast enough that you'll stop complaining?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Night and day, honestly. Full builds that used to make me go get coffee now finish before I've stood up.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Nice. Did you have to reinstall everything from scratch or did the migration tool do its thing?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Mostly a fresh install, I wanted to clean out years of junk. Took an afternoon but it felt good.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Fair enough. Anything weird come up while you were getting the toolchain working again?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Only when I was checking that our pipeline still ran from my machine. Everything we build goes through CircleCI, so I just pushed a tiny branch and watched it go green.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Good, that's the best kind of smoke test. Speaking of green, is that one flaky test still giving people grief?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Yeah, it passes nine times and then randomly fails on the tenth. I suspect it's a timing thing, but I haven't had a chance to dig in properly.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Those are the worst. People start re-running instead of investigating and then nobody trusts the suite.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Exactly. I'd rather quarantine it and fix it for real than keep hitting retry and hoping.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Agreed. Different topic, I've been meaning to ask how code review has been feeling lately. I saw a couple of pretty blunt comments go by this week.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Yeah, I noticed. I think people forget tone doesn't carry well in text, so a short comment reads colder than intended.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Right. I'd love it if we leaned toward asking questions instead of issuing verdicts, like 'what do you think about trying this' rather than 'this is wrong'.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: That's my approach too. And mentioning something that's done well in the diff costs nothing and makes the rest easier to hear.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Couldn't have said it better. Maybe I'll drop a short note about it in the team channel without calling anyone out.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Sounds good. Talk in a couple of weeks, enjoy the rest of your week!

turns.speaker: Corwin

turns.text: Oh nice. Anything interesting in the review queue?

turns.text: Maybe we carve out an hour every Friday just for docs? Nothing heroic, just chipping away.

turns.text: I'd be into that. Small and regular beats a giant cleanup sprint that never happens.

turns.text: Fair. Speaking of small annoyances, I've noticed some review comments lately that feel a bit curt. Nothing from you, just in general.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Yeah, I've seen that too. Text strips out tone, so a plain 'why is this here' can land way harder than someone intended.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Right. I'd love to nudge people toward asking questions instead of making demands, something like 'what was the thinking here?'

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: I like that. I also try to say what's good in a PR before I pick at anything, even if it's just one line.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: That's a good habit. Maybe I'll float it at the next team sync as a soft guideline rather than a rule.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Soft is the way to go. Nobody likes a rulebook about being nice, it just makes people self-conscious.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Ha, true. Okay, I should run, I've got a meeting starting in a few minutes.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: No worries. Let me know what facilities says about the coffee machine, I might bring my own beans in the meantime.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Will do. If the grinder dies for good I'm blaming you for jinxing it.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Deal. Talk soon!

turns.text: Yeah, that was my favorite part too. I might try pitching a smaller version of that idea to the team.

turns.text: Do it. Also, since you asked about infra the other day, the service is hosted in Singapore, so latency for us is fine but a bit slower for folks elsewhere.

turns.text: Got it, thanks. I'll pass that along if anyone asks.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Honestly that goes a long way. People take suggestions way better when there's a reason attached.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Right? Oh, before I forget, Priya owns the billing module, so any questions on that should go to her.

turns.text: Perfect, I'll loop her in on the thread then. Thanks for the heads up.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: No problem. One more thing, a new blocker bug was just opened on the release: the timezone drift.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Okay, thanks for flagging it. I'll keep an eye on it and check in with you next time.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Sounds good. Talk in a couple of weeks!

turns.text: Nice. Did the migration of your dev environment go smoothly, or did you lose a day to it?

turns.text: Mostly smooth. I lost an hour on some stubborn dotfiles and that was about it. Builds are noticeably faster now.

turns.text: Ah, okay, good to know. I'll fix my notes. And yes, I like the question approach for reviews, it keeps people from getting defensive.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Also, to be clear for anyone wondering, Anselm leads design on the project. That's settled.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Understood. Back to the newcomer for a sec: do you think she'd benefit from a short walkthrough of how we do reviews?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Definitely. A short doc plus a quick call would do it, and I can sit in on her next couple of reviews so she sees the tone we aim for.

turns.text: I believe it's $31,000 for the quarter.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Okay, I'll put that down. Give me a second, I'm typing it in.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Wait, hold on, I got that wrong, sorry. It's not $31,000, that was a mistake on my part. The quarterly cloud budget is $24,500.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Good catch, fixing it now. Better to sort that out before finance sees it.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Agreed. Anyway, I'll look over the invoice questions tomorrow, and Henrik handles billing module stuff now, so I'll loop him in on any of the code side.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Sounds good. Are you joining the team lunch on Friday? I think we're trying that new noodle place.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Definitely. Though I should warn you, QA just opened a new blocker on the release: the export crash.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Ugh, okay. Let's talk it through after lunch, then, so it doesn't spoil the noodles.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Fair. I'll start digging into it in the repo, kestrel-core, this afternoon so I have something to show you.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Perfect. Enjoy the new laptop and the fancy espresso in the meantime.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Hey Corwin, how's your Monday going? Mine started with way too much coffee.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Ha, same here. Busy but good. Did you get a chance to meet the new person who started last week?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Yeah, we paired for a bit on Friday. Sharp, asks good questions, and already figured out how to run everything locally.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Great, I was hoping they'd settle in quickly. I'll check in with them later this week so they don't feel lost.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Good idea. Oh, and before I forget, the duplicate invoice bug is fixed and closed. It merged this morning and nothing weird showed up after.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Nice, that's a relief. Thanks for chasing it down.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: No problem. The newcomer actually left a really polite review comment on my patch, which made me think about review manners in general.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Oh yeah? I'm a big believer in phrasing things as questions rather than orders. 'What do you think about trying X?' lands way better than 'change this'.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Totally. And praising the stuff that's actually good, not just pointing out what's wrong. People forget that part.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Agreed. Also no nitpicking on style when a linter could handle it. Saves everyone's patience.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Ha, yes. Speaking of tools, I finally got approval to upgrade my laptop. The old one sounds like a jet engine whenever I compile anything.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Finally! What are you getting? I've been eyeing a lighter one for my commute.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Something with a lot more memory and a better battery. I'm mostly excited about not having to carry the charger everywhere.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: That alone is worth it. Let me know how it feels once it arrives, I might copy your choice.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Will do. Setting it up will probably eat a whole afternoon though.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Worth it. Alright, I'll let you get back to it. Talk in a couple of weeks!

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Morning! Fair warning, I'm typing this on the new laptop and the keyboard feels completely different. I keep hitting the wrong keys.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Ha, the upgrade finally landed? How's it running compared to the old one?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Way faster. Builds that used to make me go get coffee now finish before I stand up. Migrating all my dotfiles was a pain though.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Worth it, I'd say. Anything on the Kestrel side I should know about this week?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Yeah, one thing: we moved off what we had before, and the database Kestrel runs on is now PostgreSQL. The switch went smoother than I expected.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Good to hear it was painless. I'll update the architecture overview so it doesn't say something stale.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Speaking of docs, we really have a pile of documentation debt. Half the setup guide still describes how things worked ages ago.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Yeah, I know, that one's on my conscience. Maybe we carve out a half day next sprint just for cleaning up docs?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: I'd be into that. Even just deleting the outdated pages would help a lot.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Deal. How's the pre-release testing looking overall?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Mostly on track. We do have a contract with Quillon for the load testing, so that side is covered and I don't have to build the harness myself.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Nice, that saves you a ton of time. Anything nasty turn up?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: One thing, yes. A new blocker bug got opened on the release: the sync memory leak. I only started digging into it this morning.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Okay, thanks for flagging it. Let me know if you need me to shuffle anyone's priorities to help.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Will do. Also, there's this one flaky test that fails maybe one run in ten and nobody can pin down why. It's driving me up the wall.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Classic. Flaky tests are the worst, they teach everyone to just hit rerun. Let's give it an hour of focused attention before it rots further.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Hey Dalia, how's the new laptop treating you? I heard IT finally swapped yours out.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Finally, yes! It showed up Monday and I've spent most of the week just getting my setup back to normal. The fans are way quieter though, so I'm not complaining.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Nice. Mine is due for an upgrade too but I keep putting it off because I dread the migration part.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Honestly, just write down your dotfiles and installed tools before you start. That saved me about half a day of confusion.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Good tip, I'll do that. Also, are you coming to the team lunch on Friday? I'm trying to get a headcount.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Yep, count me in. Is it still the noodle place down the street, or did people vote for something else?

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Still the noodle place. Someone suggested tacos but the noodle camp was louder.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Ha, fair enough. I'm fine with noodles, as long as they have a decent vegetarian option.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: They do, I checked the menu last time. Totally unrelated, but I've been feeling guilty about our documentation lately. So much of it is out of date.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Oh, tell me about it. I opened the setup guide last week and half the steps referenced things we stopped using ages ago.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: That's exactly the kind of thing I mean. New people hit it and lose a day just figuring out what's still real.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Maybe we could set aside an afternoon, just a docs cleanup session where everyone fixes whatever page they touched last. Small and low pressure.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: I like that. Small and scoped is the only way it'll actually happen. I'll try to find a slot that doesn't clash with anything.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Maybe pair it with the lunch? Everyone's in a good mood after noodles, so they might be more willing.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Ha, bribing people with food to write docs. Honestly, that might work better than any process I could come up with.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Worked on me every time. Alright, I'll go finish unpacking my digital life onto this laptop, talk soon!

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Hey Dalia, got a minute? I wanted to ask how your week has been going.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Pretty decent, actually. Spent a good chunk of it reviewing other people's pull requests, which got me thinking about review manners.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Oh, I'd love to hear this. What's your take?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Mostly that comments should be phrased as questions or suggestions, not commands. 'What do you think about extracting this?' lands way better than 'extract this.'

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: That makes sense. I've seen reviews that read like a scolding and the author just goes quiet for two days.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Right, and then the whole thing stalls. I also try to leave at least one genuine compliment if something's clever, otherwise it feels like a list of complaints.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Good habit. Totally unrelated, but I watched a conference talk last night about running engineering teams with less meeting overhead.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Ooh, was it any good? Those talks tend to be either super practical or just vibes.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Surprisingly practical. The speaker's big idea was that every recurring meeting should have to re-justify itself every quarter, or it gets cancelled by default.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: I like that. Most standing meetings survive purely out of inertia.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Exactly. I'm tempted to try it on my own calendar and see what's left.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Let me know how brave you get. Meanwhile I've been fighting a flaky test that fails maybe one run in twenty, and only when the machine is under load.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Ugh, those are the worst. Is it a timing thing?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Almost certainly. Something is assuming an operation finishes within a fixed window, and when things get slow it just loses the race.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Classic. Do you retry it or hunt down the real cause?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Hunt it down. Retrying just hides the problem and teaches everyone to ignore red builds, which is how real failures slip through.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Hey Dalia, how's your week going? Mine's been mostly meetings, so I'm a bit fried.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Pretty good actually. The new hire started Monday and I've been helping her get her laptop and environment sorted.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Oh nice, how's she settling in? I only met her briefly on the intro call.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: She's sharp and asks good questions, which I love. She's a bit shy in the team channel still, but that usually passes after a week or two.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Good to hear. Did she get her first pull request up yet?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Yeah, a small one yesterday, just a typo fix in a config file. I figured that's the gentlest way to learn how our review flow works.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Smart. How did the review go? I always worry newcomers get steamrolled by overly picky comments.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: That's exactly what I tried to avoid. I told the reviewers to lead with what's good, phrase suggestions as questions, and not bury her in nitpicks on a first PR.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Love that. I've seen people leave teams over a harsh review thread, so a little kindness goes a long way.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Agreed. Honestly the rest of us could stand to be nicer in reviews too, I've caught myself writing 'why would you do this' more than once.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Ha, guilty as well. Maybe we jot down a few review guidelines somewhere so it's not just tribal knowledge.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: That ties into the documentation mess, honestly. She hit three places where the setup guide was just wrong or missing steps.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Ugh, the docs debt keeps biting us. Is she willing to note down what tripped her up while it's fresh?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: She already started a list. Fresh eyes are the best docs audit you can get, so I told her to fix things as she goes.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Perfect. Let's carve out a little time next sprint to clean up the worst pages, even if it's just an afternoon.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Sounds good to me. I'll set up a short doc-cleanup session and invite her so she feels like part of it.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Hey Dalia, got a minute? Wanted to ask how the review comments have been landing lately. Someone on the team told me a few of them felt a bit blunt.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Yeah, I've heard that too. I think it's mostly tone in text, nobody means anything by it. I've started opening with what I liked before getting into the nitpicks.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: That seems like a good habit. I always think a question lands better than a command, like 'what if we tried this?' instead of 'change this.'

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Totally. Also I'm trying to stop leaving drive-by comments on PRs I don't have context for. If I'm not going to actually review it properly, I'd rather say so.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Fair. Speaking of things that annoy people, is that flaky test still acting up?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Yep, it passes three times and then fails on the fourth for no reason I can see. I suspect a timing thing, but I haven't had a clean block of time to dig in.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Ugh, those are the worst. Should we just quarantine it for now so it stops crying wolf?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Probably, as long as we leave a note and a ticket so it doesn't get forgotten. Quarantined tests have a way of becoming permanent.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: True. Oh, before I forget, I need to update the vendor list for the next status report. Anything changed on your side?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: One thing, we ended the contract with Quillon. It wrapped up cleanly, so there's nothing hanging over us there.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Got it, thanks. I'll take them off the list.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: While we're on reports, can you make sure the summary mentions that Northwind Dairy is the main client? I noticed the last one was kind of vague about who we're building this for.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Good call, I'll make that explicit. People skim those things, so clearer is better.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Same energy as our docs, honestly. We have a pile of documentation debt, half the setup guide is out of date.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: I know, and every new person trips over it. Maybe we block out one afternoon a month just for docs?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: I'd be into that. Even small fixes help, like correcting a stale command when you spot it instead of just grumbling.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Deal. I'll put a recurring slot on the calendar and we'll see if it sticks.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Hey Dalia, how's your week going? Mine's been a blur of standups.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Pretty decent, actually. I spent half of Tuesday chasing a flaky test that only fails on the second run, never the first.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Ugh, those are the worst. Did you track down what was causing it?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Mostly. It was leaning on some shared state that another test left behind. I isolated it, but I'm keeping an eye on it for a few days.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Good call. Oh, and on the design front, just so you have it straight: Marisol leads design on Kestrel, and she has the whole time.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Speaking of things I've been putting off, our docs are in rough shape. Half the setup guide still describes how things worked ages ago.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Yeah, documentation debt is sneaky. Nobody notices until a new person tries to follow it.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Exactly, and that's how I found out. I was walking the new engineer through it and we hit three dead ends in the first twenty minutes.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: How's the newcomer settling in otherwise? I've barely talked to them.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Really well. Asks good questions, and doesn't pretend to understand when they don't, which I appreciate.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: That's a great sign. Maybe have them fix the docs as they go? Fresh eyes catch the stale bits fastest.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: I was already planning that. They've started a running list of everything that tripped them up.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Perfect. Anything on your plate I should know about before the weekend?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: One thing: the timezone drift is fixed and closed. Merged it yesterday and the numbers have stayed clean since.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Nice, that one's been nagging at everyone. Thanks for seeing it through.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Happy to. Now I just need to get the flaky test fully behind me and carve out an hour for those docs.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Sounds like a plan. Enjoy the rest of your week!

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Hey Corwin, I finally watched that conference talk you sent around. The one about keeping reviews small.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Oh nice, what did you think? I thought the speaker was a bit intense but the content was solid.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Same. The bit about reviewing the code and not the person stuck with me. I've been trying to phrase my comments as questions lately.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: That's a good habit. 'What happens if this is null?' lands way softer than 'you forgot a null check.'

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Right? And it actually gets better answers sometimes, because people explain their reasoning instead of getting defensive.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: I'd add that approving fast on tiny changes matters too. Nobody wants a one-line fix sitting for three days.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Ha, true. Although I'll admit I've let a few small ones sit just because I was deep in something else.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: We all do it. Honestly a quick 'I'll look this afternoon' message helps more than silence.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Good call. Oh, unrelated, I spent half my morning chasing a flaky test. Passes nine times, fails on the tenth.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Ugh, the worst kind. Is it usually timing, or something with shared state?

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Looks like timing. Something assumes an async thing finishes before the assertion runs, and mostly it does.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Classic. Mostly works is the most dangerous phrase in testing.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Agreed. I'm going to rewrite it to wait on the actual condition instead of sleeping for a fixed bit.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Yes, please. Fixed sleeps are just flakiness with extra steps.

turns.speaker: Dalia
turns.text: Ha, I'm stealing that line for my next review comment. Phrased as a question, of course.

turns.speaker: Corwin
turns.text: Perfect. Talk again in a couple of weeks, enjoy the rest of your Sunday!

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Morning Petra, hope your week has started better than mine. Inbox is a disaster.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Morning! Same here, honestly. Took me an hour just to dig out from the weekend.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Have you heard anything from Marlow's side since we last spoke?

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Not a word. They're taking days to answer even simple emails, it's getting a bit ridiculous.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Ha, that's about what I expected. They took nearly a week to confirm a meeting room last time.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: I'll chase them again today. By the way, the liability cap is $2 million, just so you have that figure in front of you.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Okay, good to have it in writing. Thanks for flagging.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: No problem. Should we pencil in another call for early next month?

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Works for me. Mornings are better, I'm usually stuck in meetings after lunch.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Mornings it is. I'll send over a couple of slots later this week.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Perfect. Oh, my office is closed for the holiday on Monday, so I'll be offline that day.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Ours too, the whole firm shuts down. Nothing will move on my end until Tuesday.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Fine by me, it's not like Marlow will notice anyway given how slow they are.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Ha, true. If they do reply over the break, I'll deal with it when I'm back.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Sounds good. Enjoy the long weekend then.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: You too, Yusuf. Talk soon!

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Morning Yusuf! How was your weekend? Did you manage to get any rest?

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Morning! Mostly yes, though I spent Sunday going through some old files and found the paperwork from that distribution deal we did years ago. Remember the one with the very stubborn counterparty?

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Ha, how could I forget. We went through something like nine drafts of one paragraph. I still think we won that argument on points.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: We did, barely. Anyway, good reminder of why I like having you on this one too.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Flattery noted. Speaking of this one, the liability cap has changed and is now $750,000.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Okay, good to know. I'll flag it to our finance people this week so they're not caught off guard.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Sounds good. By the way, are you still planning to have me visit the plant? You mentioned it last time.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Yes, definitely. Come out in a couple of weeks if you can. I'd love for you to see the production floor, it helps to understand what we're actually protecting in all this paperwork.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: I'd like that. I'll check my calendar and send a few slots. Should I bring boots or is it more of a hard hat and lanyard situation?

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Hard hat and safety glasses, we'll supply both. Just wear shoes you don't mind getting a bit dusty.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Perfect. Oh, and a heads up that my office closes for a few days over the holiday coming up, so I'll be slow to reply then.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Noted. We shut the plant that same stretch, so honestly I'll be offline too. Before that, one thing I wanted to mention: the agreement includes an exclusivity clause, and I want to make sure we talk it through properly.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Fair enough, let's put time aside for it soon. I'll come to the plant visit with questions ready.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Great, that works for me. I'll have our operations lead join so you can ask him anything directly.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Wonderful. I'll send those calendar slots later today.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Thanks Petra. Talk soon!

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Hi Yusuf, quick one before we get into it: our office is shut next Friday for the holiday, so if you need me then, shoot me a message before Thursday evening.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Noted, thanks. Honestly I'm planning to be offline most of that day anyway.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Good plan. On the draft, the delivery clause now names Antwerp as where the goods get dropped off.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Okay, that works for our logistics people. Did Marlow say anything about the draft yet?

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Not a word. It's been almost ten days since I sent my last email and I've had nothing back, not even an acknowledgement.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Ugh, typical. They took forever last time too, I remember waiting over a week just for a one-line answer.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: I'll chase them again tomorrow morning. If they keep stalling we may need to put a soft deadline on their response.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Fine by me. One thing I wanted to confirm so we're on the same page: the agreement runs under Ontario law.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Got it, I'll keep that in mind as I go through their comments when they finally arrive.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Also, the minimum we commit to each year is 55,000 units. That's settled on our side, no more debating it internally.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Understood, I'll treat that as fixed from here on.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: And for payment, we're going with 45 days.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Great, that's clear. Should we book the next call for the week after the closure? I'm fairly open on Tuesday or Wednesday.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Wednesday afternoon is better for me, I've got a standing meeting Tuesday.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Wednesday afternoon it is. I'll send over an invite shortly.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Perfect, talk then. Enjoy the long weekend!

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Hey Petra, quick one before the weekend. Is your office closed over the Easter break? I want to know when I can reach you.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: We close from the Thursday before Easter through the Monday after. I'll still check email once a day, so nothing will sit for long.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Good to know. By the way, I've been meaning to ask: the person who signs for Marlow Ltd is Ms. Devereux, so you can put her name in the signature block.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Noted, I'll draft it that way. Are you free for a call next week to walk through the latest draft?

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Yes, Wednesday afternoon works. Also, you should come and see the plant sometime. We just reorganised the whole floor and it looks completely different.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: I'd love that, I haven't been out there in ages. Maybe after the Easter break, once things calm down.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Sounds good. Oh, and I need to fix something I told you earlier. I made a mistake, the person signing for Marlow Ltd is not Ms. Devereux. It's Mr. Nakagawa.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: No problem, glad you caught it before it went anywhere. I'll update the signature block today.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
turns.text: Thanks. One more correction while I'm at it. I said Ontario law for the agreement, and that was wrong. It's Swiss law.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Okay, thanks for flagging it. I'll adjust the draft accordingly and send you a clean copy.

turns.speaker: Yusuf
