turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Oh good, I'd rather get it done early. Last year half the street was coughing by October.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Exactly, better to be ahead of it. Enjoy the rest of the week and give that granddaughter a wave from me!

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Will do, thanks Noor. Speak soon.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Hi Edmund, it's Noor from the practice. How's your week been so far?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Hi Noor, not bad at all, thanks. Bit muggy out but I can't complain.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Glad to hear it. Did the appointment reminder text come through okay last week? We changed the system and I wanted to check people are actually getting them.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Yes, it came through fine. Pinged my phone the day before, which is just about right for me.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Perfect, that's what it's meant to do. Have you been keeping up with the walking?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: More or less, yes. I've been going out most mornings before it gets hot, just round the park and back.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: That's great, little and often is the best way. Do you feel any difference from it?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: I sleep better, I'll say that. Oh, and I should tell you, the doctor I'm under is Dr. Sato now. Dr. Patel moved on or something, and I got a letter about it.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Thanks for letting me know, I'll make sure that's noted on my side too. Has the change been okay for you?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Seems fine so far. Also, my physio is all done. They said I was finished and stopped the sessions, so I've got my Tuesdays back.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Good news, well done for sticking with it. Enjoy the free Tuesdays!

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Ha, I will. Probably spend them walking, to be honest.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Sounds like a plan. Now, flu season is creeping up, so we'll be putting out the jab invitations in a few weeks. Have you had one in previous years?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Every year, yes. I'd rather get it early than catch the thing, so just text me when the slots open.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Will do, it'll come as one of those text reminders. Anything else you wanted to chat about today?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: No, that's everything from me. Thanks for checking in, Noor.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Any time, Edmund. Take care and I'll be in touch again in a couple of weeks.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Hi Edmund, it's Noor from the practice. How are you getting on this week?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Hello Noor, not bad at all, thanks. Bit tired today but nothing to complain about.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Glad to hear it. Just so you know before your next visit, the lift at the clinic is out of order again.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Oh no, not again. Is it the one by the main entrance? I'm not sure my knees would love the stairs.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Yes, that one. If stairs are a problem we can book you into one of the ground floor rooms instead, just say the word.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: That would be kind, thank you. And what about parking? Last time I circled the car park for ages.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: It does get busy mid-morning. Early appointments are easier, and there's usually space round the back if the front lot is full.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Good tip. I'll ask for an early slot then. Saves me the stress of hunting for a space.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Sensible plan. How have you been finding things day to day? Are you getting out much?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Actually yes, I've been walking more lately. Nothing fancy, just round the block after dinner and a bit further at weekends.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: That's brilliant, Edmund. Little and often really adds up, and it's good that it fits into your routine.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: It's growing on me, honestly. The evenings are still light enough that it feels pleasant rather than a chore.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Lovely. Keep that going while the weather's kind, and don't be too hard on yourself on the rainy days.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Ha, I'll try not to. I might even drag my neighbour along, she's been saying she needs to get out more too.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Even better, company makes it easier to stick with. I'll let you know about the lift when I hear more from the front desk.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Thanks Noor, I appreciate it. Speak to you in a couple of weeks.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Morning Edmund! How's your week been going?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Not bad at all, thanks Noor. Sleeping a bit better lately, I'm only waking up once in the night instead of three or four times.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Oh that's good to hear. Any idea what's made the difference?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: I think it's cutting out the late cup of tea, and the evening walks help too. My granddaughter's been staying over on weekends and she wears me out in the best way.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Ha, that'll do it! How old is she now?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: She's just turned seven and she's obsessed with drawing. Last Saturday she did a portrait of me with enormous ears, so I've got that stuck on the fridge now.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: That sounds lovely. I'd frame it if I were you.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Might do. Anyway, I got the letter through about my bloods, 6.4%, and then spent most of the afternoon hunting for the flu jab leaflet that came in the same envelope.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Ah yes, flu clinics are starting up now. It's worth booking one in soon, the season usually picks up from October.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: I'll ring the surgery tomorrow. My neighbour had a dreadful bout last winter and was flat on his back for two weeks, so I'm not taking chances.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Very sensible. Are you keeping up with the walks even when the weather turns?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Mostly, yes, I just wrap up warm. Oh, and I meant to say, I stopped taking the vitamin D a few weeks back, I kept forgetting it anyway.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Okay, thanks for letting me know, I'll make a note of that.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Right you are. Do you get a flu jab yourself, being around poorly people all day?

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Always, first in the queue. Anything else on your mind before I let you go?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: No, I think that's me. Say hello to everyone at the surgery, and I'll speak to you in a couple of weeks.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Hi Edmund, it's Noor from the practice. Just checking in like we do. How are you getting on this week?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Hello Noor. Not bad at all, can't complain. Tired today though, didn't sleep brilliantly last night.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Oh no, was it a restless night or more waking up and not getting back off?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Mostly waking up around three and staring at the ceiling. I was out like a light before that, so it's the middle bit that gets me.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: That's really common, annoyingly. Has it been like that most nights lately, or just the odd one?

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Odd one, mostly. The last week or so has actually been better than it was a while back. I think the cooler evenings help.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: That's good to hear. Cooler rooms do tend to help people drop off and stay off.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Right, I'll keep the window cracked then. By the way, I was at the clinic last week and the parking was a nightmare. I drove round three times before I found a space.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Ha, sorry about that. It fills up fast in the mornings, especially on the busy clinic days. Afternoons are usually much easier if you can swing it.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Good tip, I'll try an afternoon next time. And then I got in and the lift was out of order. Had to haul myself up the stairs.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Yes, that lift has been playing up. I'm told an engineer is coming to sort it, though I'll believe it when I see it working.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Fair enough. The stairs did me no harm, mind you, though I was puffing a bit at the top.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Well, a bit of stair climbing never hurt anyone. Just take it steady if the lift's still out when you're next in.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Will do. Anyway, nothing else much to report from me this time. Quiet few weeks.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Quiet is good! Thanks for the chat, Edmund. I'll check in again in a couple of weeks, and do ring the practice if anything comes up before then.

turns.speaker: Edmund
turns.text: Brilliant, thanks Noor. Speak soon, and I'll let you know how the sleeping goes.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning Leandro! Did you see the window display when you walked past last night? I finally swapped the old banner for the new frame we found in the back.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: I did, it looks loads better. The red frame really catches your eye from across the road.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: That was the idea. I might hang a few helmets off the handlebars too, make it look a bit more lived in.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Good call. Maybe add a little sign about the race on Saturday week? Half the club is doing it.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ha, yes, the local ten-mile thing. Are you riding it or just standing at the finish with a flask?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Flask, definitely. My legs haven't recovered from the last time I tried to keep up with those lot.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Fair enough. Oh, before I forget, I've got a couple of online orders to pack up this afternoon. Those all go out with Parcelwing, so the labels are in the drawer under the counter.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Got it, I'll sort them after lunch. Is the big box for the wheelset still sitting by the door?

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: That's the one. Wrap it well, it's a long way to travel.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Will do. By the way, we've had loads of people in with punctures since the roadworks started on the high street.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: I noticed! It must be all the grit and bits of metal they've left in the gutter. Three people came in on Monday alone.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: I've been telling everyone to check their tyres for embedded stuff before they ride off. Most of them just shrug.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Maybe we should put a note by the till about it. Something friendly, not preachy.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: I can scribble one up with a little drawing of a sad tyre. Customers like that sort of thing.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Perfect, do it. Right, kettle's on, want a tea before we open?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Yes please, two sugars. I'll get the sign started while it brews.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning Leandro. Did you see the van parked right across our door again? I had to squeeze in sideways with my coffee.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Ha, yes. I got in early and it was already there, engine running and nobody in sight. I went and knocked on the cafe next door and it turned out to be theirs.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Of course it was. Did they at least say sorry?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: The driver came out looking sheepish and moved it about ten minutes later. I think he'll think twice next week.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Good. Anyway, I've been meaning to ask if you're still up for the charity ride next month? I told the organisers we'd put a little stand out.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Definitely, I'm in. I'll bring the foldable gazebo from my garage so we're not standing in the rain like last time.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Brilliant, last time my sandwich went soggy and I've not forgiven the weather since.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Fair enough. Do you think we should do a quick free safety check for anyone riding? People always turn up with a flat or a loose saddle.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Yes, love that idea. It's good for the riders and people see us doing something useful.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Also, are you going to the local race on Saturday? A couple of the regulars are entering and I promised I'd cheer them on.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: I'm hoping to pop along for an hour or so. I'll bring a flask and a loud voice.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Perfect, the loud voice is half the job. The course goes up that nasty hill by the church, so it should be a good one to watch.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Oh that hill is brutal. I'll be shouting extra loud there then.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Ha, they'll need it. Should I keep an eye out for that van again before we open tomorrow?

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Yes please, and if it's back you have my full permission to stand in front of it dramatically.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Deal. I'll bring my most disapproving face.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning! Did you see the sign-up sheet for the Saturday race? Half the club's already put their names down.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: I did, it's going to be a busy week. People will want their bikes checked over before it.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Yeah, and a couple of folks asked me yesterday what we charge, so just so we're on the same page, a basic service is $60 and that's not changing.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Got it, I'll tell anyone who asks. Do you want me to put a little card up by the counter too?

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Good idea, nothing fancy, just something handwritten. Also did you hear about the charity ride next month?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: The one for the children's hospital? My cousin is doing the long route, she's been training all winter.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: That's the one. I thought we could put out a collection jar and maybe offer to check tyre pressures for the riders on the morning.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Happy to do that. I can come in early if you want, the start's not far from the shop anyway.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Brilliant, thank you. Oh, and that delivery van was blocking the door again yesterday, I had to ask the driver to move twice.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Ha, I saw him when I came in this morning, parked right across the entrance with the hazards on. A customer nearly turned back.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: I'm going to mention it to Mrs. Pemberton, since she's our landlord and the loading bay out back is hers. Maybe she can have a word with the neighbours about where vans should stop.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: That would help a lot. The bay is always empty while the vans sit out front.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Exactly. Anyway, can you open up on Friday? I've got a dentist appointment first thing.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Sure, no problem. I'll sweep the pavement too and keep the door propped so it's obvious we're open.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: You're a star. I'll bring pastries to make up for it.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Now you're talking. See you tomorrow!

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning! Sorry, I'm running about ten minutes late. There's a delivery van parked right across the shop door and the driver has vanished.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Ha, I saw it when I came in. I squeezed past by the bins. Want me to go and look for him?

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Give it five minutes, he'll turn up. Did the kettle get sorted? I swear it was making that clicking noise again yesterday.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Still clicking, but it boils. I gave the limescale a go with vinegar, didn't help much. Might just be on its last legs.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ugh. Fine, we'll get a new one before it dies mid-brew. Oh, and the van guy did come back, he's moving it now. Also, a box came in earlier and it's the Ribble Hybrid, finally, so it's sitting out the back waiting to be built up.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Oh nice, that was a long wait. I'll make a start on it after I've dealt with the repair queue.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: No rush, do the repairs first. How did it go yesterday afternoon after I left? I felt bad dumping that grumpy man on you.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Ha, the one who wanted his wheel trued for nothing because he'd 'only had it a week'? He wasn't happy.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: That's him. Did he calm down at all?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Eventually. I explained it was a bent rim from hitting a kerb, not a build fault, and he went quiet. Then he asked if we could still look at it today.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Of course he did. Is he coming in this morning, then?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Said he'd be here around eleven. I'll put the wheel on the stand ready so it's not a long wait.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Good plan. If he starts up again, just call me over and I'll take him. I'm better at the smiling-through-gritted-teeth thing.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Deal. I'll stick the kettle on now, though. Might as well enjoy it while it still works.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Make mine strong. I'll be there in two minutes, just finding somewhere to park now the van's gone.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning! Did you see the van parked right across our door when you came in? It's been there since before I opened up.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Yeah, I had to squeeze past the wing mirror to get the key in. I went and knocked on the cab window but nobody was in it.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Typical. If it's still there at ten I'll ring the number on the side of it.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Fair enough. By the way, I was going through the paperwork folder yesterday and the monthly rent on the shop is $2,350, in case you wanted it for the spreadsheet.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Oh good, thanks for checking that. I always forget to write it down anywhere I can actually find it.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: No worries. Also, I was thinking we should redo the window display this week. The sun has bleached the blue backdrop and it looks a bit sad now.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Agreed, it's looking tired. Could you swap the fabric for the green one from the back cupboard? I'd like the red commuter bike front and centre.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Sure, I'll do it after lunch when it's quiet. I'll wipe the glass inside and out too, it's covered in finger smudges.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Perfect. And a customer asked me yesterday if we're open at the weekend, so I told her we're open on Sundays too, just so you know if anyone asks you.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Good to know, I'll tell people the same. Do you want me to put a little sign in the window about it while I'm in there?

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Yes please, that's a nice idea. Something simple, black marker on white card is fine.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Will do. I'm also planning to give the workshop a proper clean on Friday. There's so much grease on the floor by the stand that I nearly slipped yesterday.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ha, please don't do yourself an injury. The shop first opened in 2011 and I swear some of that grease has been there since the very first week.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: That doesn't surprise me at all. I'll bring a stiff brush and some degreaser and see what I can shift.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Brilliant, I'll buy us both a coffee on Friday as a reward. Right, I'm going to see if that van has finally moved.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Good luck! Shout if you need me to go out and glare at the driver.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning Leandro. Did you get a chance to look at the kettle? It's making that grinding noise again.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Yeah I had a go yesterday. I think it's just limescale, I ran vinegar through it twice and it's quieter now.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Brilliant, you're a hero. I was about to give up and buy a new one.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Don't throw it out yet, give it a week. If it starts again we'll bin it.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Deal. How was the afternoon, by the way? I felt bad leaving you on your own with the man who came in about the wheel.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Ha, the one who kept insisting it was our fault the rim was bent? He came back twice. I just kept nodding and offering to look at it again.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: That's about the best you can do with him. He did the same to me last year, it's never anyone's fault but ours.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: He left in a better mood in the end, said he'd think about it. I'm not holding my breath.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Fair enough. Anyway, I wanted to ask about the window. I'm thinking it's looking tired, the same bikes have been in there since February.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Agreed, it's a bit flat. The sun's bleached that cardboard backdrop too, it's gone sort of beige.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Spring display, then. Something with a bit of colour, maybe a couple of bikes angled towards the street instead of lined up like soldiers.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: I like that. I could grab some plants from the market on Saturday and put a few round the wheels, makes it look less like a warehouse.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Yes please, keep the receipt and I'll sort you out. Nothing too fussy though, we don't want anything dripping on the paintwork.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Plastic pots on a tray, nothing dripping. I'll sketch it out and send you a photo before I move anything.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Perfect. I'll be in after lunch, so leave the old display until I'm there and we'll do it together.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Sounds good. I'll put the kettle on for when you arrive, assuming it survives.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning! Did you see the road race went right past the end of our street on Saturday? Half the riders looked like they were suffering already.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Ha, I caught the tail end of it on my way in. Someone had a puncture right outside the bakery and I nearly ran out with a pump.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: You should have! Free advertising. Anyway, are you still up for the charity ride next month?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Definitely, I've already told my cousin he's coming too. He hasn't ridden in years so I'll be waiting for him at every hill.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Good, bring snacks then. I thought we could do a little tune-up stand at the start for anyone with squeaky brakes.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Nice idea. Oh, before I forget, I was sorting the paperwork folder yesterday and the rent letter came through, so the shop's monthly rent is now $1,950.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ah, right. I'd been expecting something like that, thanks for flagging it. I'll sort it out with the accounts this week.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: No rush, I just didn't want it sitting in the folder. How did the afternoon go yesterday, by the way? I left before the man with the folding bike came back.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Oh, don't. He came back twice and argued that the fault was the road, not his bike. Then he asked for a discount for his trouble.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Classic. Did you give him one?

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Not a penny, but I did give him a cup of tea so he'd stop sighing at the counter. He left almost smiling.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: That's your superpower, honestly. I'd have just handed him the spanner and said good luck.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Oh, one good bit of news, a new e-bike arrived in stock this morning: the Trek Verve. It's sitting by the window if you want to have a look.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Nice, I'll pop it on a stand and give it a proper once-over after lunch. The window display could do with something shiny anyway.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Perfect. Maybe wipe off the fingerprints from the last customer who pressed his nose against the glass.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Will do. I'll leave the nose prints on the charity ride poster though, that's part of its charm.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning Leandro. The kettle's finally died, I've been boiling water in a saucepan like a caveman.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Ha, I wondered why the tea tasted faintly of burnt metal yesterday. We could just grab a cheap one from the shop on the corner.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Good plan, I'll pick one up at lunch. Also there's a delivery van parked right across our door again.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: I saw that. The driver was just standing there on his phone, so I knocked on his window and he moved eventually.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Brilliant, thank you. By the way, for the order sheet, our inner tubes come from Tandem Supply Co, so put that down for the next batch.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Okay, noted. Are we still doing the big clean of the workshop today or is it too busy?

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Let's do it, the floor by the stands is covered in old grease and bits of rubber. I'll sort the bench if you take the floor.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Deal. I'll get the degreaser and the stiff brush out, that stuff never comes off with just a mop.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Wait, I've got something wrong, scrap what I said earlier. Our inner-tube supplier isn't Tandem Supply Co, that was a mistake on my part. It's Spindle & Co.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Ah, glad you said before I filled anything in. I'll cross the other one out.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Thanks. I always muddle the two names when I'm tired.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Easily done. Right, I'm starting on the floor, the van's gone now so at least we can prop the door open for the fumes.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Good call. Fresh air will help, and I'll put the saucepan on for tea once we're done.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Perfect. Should I sweep the corner behind the tool wall too? There's years of dust back there.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Yes please, if you can face it. Wear a mask, it's properly grim behind there.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Will do. I'll message you when it's finished and we can celebrate with the worst cup of tea ever.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning! I finally changed the window display last night. Took me ages to get the wheel garland to hang straight.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Oh nice, I saw it on my way past. It looks really good from the street, very eye-catching.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Thanks. Quick thing before I forget: the till software we use is TillPoint, so if you're ever stuck at the counter, that's the one to look up.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Okay, good to know. I'll keep that in mind for when it freezes on me again.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Wait, sorry, I got that wrong. It's not TillPoint, that was a mistake on my part. The till software we use is ShopKeep One.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Ha, no worries. Thanks for catching it.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: How's the workshop looking? I was thinking we should do a proper deep clean this week.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Honestly it's overdue. There's chain grease on practically every surface, and the floor by the stand is properly black.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Right, let's do it Tuesday when it's quiet. Kofi is our lead mechanic, so I'll ask him to sort the tool wall while we scrub the floor.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Sounds like a plan. I'll bring some extra rags and that degreaser spray.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Perfect. Have you had many people in with punctures since the roadworks started on the high street?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Loads. Three came in on Saturday alone, all picked up glass or bits of grit from the diggings.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ugh, I thought so. Maybe we should put a little sign up reminding people to check their tyres after riding through there.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Good idea, I can write one up this afternoon and stick it by the door.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Oh, and one more thing: a new e-bike arrived in stock this morning, the red Cube. It's still in the back, so give it a wipe down before it goes on the floor.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Will do! I'll get it set up tomorrow and tuck it in near the window.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning Leandro! Did you see the charity ride is happening next month? Half the village seems to have signed up already.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: I saw the poster in the cafe window. I might do the shorter loop if my knees agree to it.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ha, your knees are twenty-six, they'll cope. I'm thinking of offering free tyre checks for anyone riding it.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Good idea, people always turn up with soft tyres and a prayer. We could do it the Saturday before.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Done, I'll put it on the chalkboard. Oh, and the red Cube was sold, a guy came in yesterday afternoon and rode away on it after about ten minutes.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Ah nice, that one had been sitting by the window for ages. The gap in the display looks odd now though.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: I'll shuffle things round tomorrow so it doesn't look so bare. Did you hear about the local race, by the way?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: The one up on the hill road? My mate Dai is entering, he's been training like mad and boring everyone about it.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Tell him to pop in beforehand and I'll check his brakes. That climb is nasty on the descent.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Will do. Speaking of nasty, I've had so many punctures coming in since the roadworks started on the high street.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Same here, three people this week alone. All of them said there was grit and bits of metal left in the gutter.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: I rode through it on Friday and picked up a sliver of glass. Took me ages to find it in the tyre.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Maybe we should ring the council and ask them to sweep it properly. It's costing everyone a fortune in patches.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Good call, I'll email them this afternoon if you like. Might get a faster reply from the shop address than from me.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Yes, use the shop one, thanks. I'll bring biscuits in tomorrow as a thank you for covering the counter.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Now you're talking. See you in the morning!

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning Leandro! Did you manage to sort the kettle out? It was making that awful rattling noise again yesterday.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Morning! I descaled it last night, so it should be quieter now. Fingers crossed, otherwise it's going in the bin.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ha, brilliant. I'll test it with a proper cuppa as soon as I'm in.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Oh, before I forget, we ship the online orders with Dropswift now. The old courier stopped collecting from us, so I switched it over on Thursday.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Good to know, thanks for sorting that. Are the labels printing okay?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Yep, printed three this morning without any trouble. Easier than before, honestly.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Lovely. Are you still coming along to the charity ride on Saturday week? I promised the organisers we'd have someone on hand for punctures.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Definitely, I'll bring the pump and a bag of patches. Do you think I'll need the track pump too, or just the mini one?

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Bring both, people always turn up with soft tyres. And we do rent bikes out, so a few folks might ask us about hiring one on the day.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Good point, I'll make a little sign for the van so people know. Might even get a few new faces in the shop out of it.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Fingers crossed. Right, the workshop is a state again, there's oil on the floor and the bench is buried.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: I can do a proper clean this afternoon once the morning rush dies down. I'll do the degreaser tray and sweep under the stands as well.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: You're a star. Oh, and the Orbea Vibe came in this morning, so it's sitting by the window now.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Nice, it looks smart in the photos. I'll wipe it down and put it out front once the workshop is done.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Perfect. See you in a bit, and save me a decent mug if that kettle behaves!

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Will do, see you soon!

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning Leandro! Did you see the turnout for the local race on Saturday? The whole high street was lined with people.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: I did, I walked past on my way to the bakery. Loads of kids on the sidelines banging pots and pans, it was brilliant.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ha, sounds about right. Oh, before I forget, we're shipping the online orders with Harrier Post now, so the old labels in the drawer are no good any more.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Got it, I'll bin the old ones and keep an eye out for the new packaging. Do I need to do anything different when I book a pickup?

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Nope, same routine, just a different name on the box. Pretty painless really.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Good. Are we still on for the charity ride next month? I'm trying to talk my brother into coming along.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Definitely. I'd love to get a decent group from the shop together, maybe we could set up a little water stop outside the door as it passes.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Great idea. I can bring a few folding chairs and a banner if you've got spare card to make a sign.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: I've got plenty of card. Also, a bit of admin news: the rent on the shop is $2,800 a month now, so I'll be watching the budget a little closer.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Ah, fair enough. Let me know if there's anything I can do on my end to help keep costs down.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Will do, thanks. Honestly just keep being brilliant with the customers and we'll be fine.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Easy enough. Oh, the kettle in the back is making that rattling noise again, I think the element is going.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ugh, that kettle has been through the wars. I'll grab a new one this week, we can't be without tea.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Honestly it's the most important piece of equipment in the building. Right after the pump, maybe.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ha, agreed. By the way, the Cannondale Tesoro turned up this morning, it's the new one in the corner by the window.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Oh nice, I'll go and give it a wipe down and put the tag on it. Cuppa first, assuming the kettle survives the morning!

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning! How did the weekend go in the shop? I only managed to pop in on Saturday afternoon.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Busy, mostly. We had a run of punctures come in, all from people who'd ridden through the roadworks on the main road.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ha, I had a feeling that would happen. Was it all glass and bits of grit?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Mostly little flints and a couple of staples. One guy had three in the same tyre, he was not thrilled.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Poor thing. Did you put a note by the till about checking tyres for embedded bits before fitting a new tube? Saves people coming straight back.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Yeah, I stuck one up on Friday. Most people actually read it, which surprised me.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Good. Oh, and Saoirse is the lead mechanic now, so if anything technical comes up while I'm out, ask her first. Anyway, did the man with the creaky bottom bracket ever come back?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: He did, and he was a nightmare. Said we hadn't fixed it, then admitted he'd been riding a different bike the whole time.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Oh no, classic. Did he at least apologise?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Sort of. He muttered something and bought a bottle of chain lube on the way out, so I'll count that as a win.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ha, a peace offering. By the way, the Trek Verve was sold on Saturday, just before I left. Can you take it off the website and the window card?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Nice one, will do this morning. Was it the lady who'd been back twice to look at it?

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: That's the one. She finally decided, and she was really happy with it.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Great. I was thinking of giving the workshop a proper clean on Wednesday when it's quiet, the floor by the stand is properly black.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Yes please, that would be brilliant. Just don't throw out the old rags in the blue box, I use those for the mudguards.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Ha, noted, blue box stays. I'll shove everything else on the shelves into the cupboard while I mop.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning! Did you see the road closures for Saturday's race? The whole high street is going to be taped off by nine.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Yeah, I saw the notice on the lamppost. Should be a good crowd though, maybe a few people will wander in.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Fingers crossed. I might put a sign out front just in case.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Good idea. Oh, by the way, the rent on the shop has changed, it's now $2,100 a month. Letter came through yesterday.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ah, right. Thanks for letting me know, I'll sort it out when I'm in tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: No rush, it doesn't start till next month anyway.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Okay good. Anyway, the workshop is a state. I was thinking we could do a proper clean on Friday afternoon.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Fine by me. The floor by the back bench is properly grim, there's chain oil everywhere.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ha, I know. I'll bring some of that degreaser spray from home, it works better than what we've got.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Perfect. I'll sort the tool wall while I'm at it, half the spanners are in the wrong spots.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: You're a star. Is the kettle still doing that weird clicking thing?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Worse, now it takes ages to boil and then switches off halfway. I think it's finally dying.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ugh. I'll grab a new one on my way in, can't run a workshop without tea.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Definitely not. Get a cheap one though, ours gets descaled about once a year.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ha, fair point. Right, I'll see you tomorrow, I'll bring biscuits too.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Brilliant, see you then!

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning! Did you see the window display when you came past? I swapped the helmets around yesterday evening.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: I did, looks much better. The blue ones catch the light nicely now.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Good, that was the idea. Though I couldn't hang the banner properly because of that delivery van parked right across the door.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Ha, I saw it this morning too. The driver was nowhere to be found for ages, I had to squeeze in sideways with the bags.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Typical. Is the kettle behaving, by the way? It was making a weird clicking noise on Thursday.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Still clicking, but it boils. I'd give it another month before it gives up completely.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: I'll pick up a new one if it dies. Can't run this place without tea.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Agreed. Oh, a customer asked me yesterday what we charge, and I told him a basic service is $55, which is what it's always been.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Right. Anyway, I moved the little stand with the bells closer to the counter, did you notice?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: I did, people keep picking them up and ringing them. Constant jingling all afternoon.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Good for sales, bad for my ears. Someone rang on the phone yesterday asking about hiring a bike for the weekend, by the way.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Oh, what did you tell them?

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: That we've stopped offering rentals. They were a bit disappointed but said they'd try elsewhere.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Fair enough. Want me to move the display stand away from the window so the sun doesn't fade the boxes?

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Yes please, and put the kettle on while you're back there. I'll take the van driver a stern look when he finally turns up.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Deal. Tea first, stern looks second.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Morning! Did you see the sign-up numbers for the charity ride? Way more than last year.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: I did, it's looking great. I think the new route through the villages helped, people like a bit of scenery.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Agreed. I'm thinking of putting a little repair stand at the halfway stop, just in case anyone gets a puncture or a loose chain.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Good idea. I can run it if you like, I don't mind giving up a Saturday morning for that.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: You're a star. Honestly I need the break from yesterday, that customer who came in twice about the same squeaky brake was a lot.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Oh no, the one in the green jacket? He cornered me last week too and kept insisting the squeak was our fault.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: That's him. I checked it three times and it was fine, I think he just likes a chat and a complaint.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Probably lonely, bless him. Still, I'm not volunteering for round three.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Fair enough, I'll take him next time. Are you riding in the local race next weekend, by the way?

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Thinking about it. My legs aren't convinced yet, I've barely trained since the summer got busy.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Ha, same excuse every year and then you finish in the top ten anyway.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Top fifteen at best! But yes, I'll probably enter. It's only a few laps round the park.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: Go on then, I'll come and heckle from the finish line with a flask of tea.

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Deal. If I'm last, you're buying the cake afterwards.

turns.speaker: Ffion
turns.text: If you're last I'll buy two. Right, I'd better unlock the stockroom, talk later!

turns.speaker: Leandro
turns.text: Speak soon, and I'll sort the repair stand kit before the ride.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Hey you! Happy new year, belatedly. How's January treating you so far?

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Happy new year! It's been slow and grey, but I'm not complaining. I've mostly been hiding indoors with tea and podcasts.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Ooh, podcasts. Anything good? I'm in a rut and keep relistening to the same three shows.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: There's a history one I've been hooked on, about forgotten sea routes and the people who ran them. Sounds dry but the host is hilarious.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Okay, that actually sounds right up my street. Is it one of those where each episode stands alone, or do you have to start at the beginning?

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: You can jump in anywhere, honestly. I started in the middle and just worked backwards.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Perfect, I'll try one on my commute tomorrow. Have you watched anything good lately? I finally saw that quiet drama everyone was raving about last year.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: The one with the lighthouse keeper? I keep meaning to. Was it worth the hype?

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Mostly yes. It's very slow and the ending is a bit ambiguous, but the cinematography is gorgeous. I wanted to argue about it with someone afterwards.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Ha, well save your arguments for me then, I'll watch it this weekend. I've been rewatching old comedies instead, which is peak comfort-zone behaviour.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: No shame in that, January is for comfort. Though all this gloom has me daydreaming about a holiday.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Same! I keep flip-flopping between somewhere hot with nothing to do and somewhere with mountains and lots of walking.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Why not both? A week of lazing by water, then a few days of hiking somewhere cooler.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Greedy, but I like it. Maybe we should both pick somewhere for later in the year and compare notes.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Deal. I'll start collecting ideas and send you a shortlist. Nothing too ambitious, I just want a good view and a decent breakfast.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: That's honestly all I need from a trip too. Speak in a couple of weeks?

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Definitely. Enjoy the lighthouse film, and tell me what you think of the ending!

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Hey you! How's the week been treating you so far?

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Pretty good actually, just busy. I finally watched that slow Korean film everyone kept recommending last weekend.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Oh nice, how was it? I started it once and fell asleep twenty minutes in.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Ha, fair, it does take its time. But the last half hour completely won me over, I was a bit of a mess by the end.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Okay, now I have to give it another go. Did you hear that Mikkel and Freja finally set a date for the wedding?

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: I did! Summer, right? I'm already trying to figure out how to get there from Aarhus without it taking all day.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Yeah, late June I think. We could probably travel together if the timing works out.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: That would be great, way less boring than going alone. Are you doing the speech thing, or is that someone else's job?

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: God, I hope not. Freja's brother is apparently already writing something, so I'm hoping I'm off the hook.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Smart. Stay quiet and nobody will think to ask you.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: That's the plan. Anyway, I've been listening to this podcast about old shipwrecks on my commute, and it's weirdly addictive.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Shipwrecks? That sounds oddly specific. Is it more history or more mystery?

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Bit of both. Each episode picks one wreck and goes through what went wrong, and the host has this very calm voice that makes everything sound worse somehow.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Haha, I love that. Send me the name, I need something new for my walks.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Will do, I'll message it over later tonight. Let me know what you think after a couple of episodes.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Deal. And you owe me a report on whether you ever finish that film.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Fine, fine. Talk in a couple of weeks!

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Hey! Did you end up doing that trail you were talking about last time? The one with the ridge section?

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Yes, finally, on Saturday. The ridge was gorgeous but the last stretch was pure mud, my boots are still sitting on the porch drying out.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Ha, classic. Was it busy up there or did you have it mostly to yourselves?

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Pretty quiet, we passed maybe four other groups the whole day. I'd go back in spring when it's drier.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Spring sounds right. Honestly I'm just tired this week, the neighbour upstairs has been dragging furniture around at like midnight.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Oh no, that's the worst. Have you said anything to them or are you still in the passive-aggressive sigh phase?

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Still in the sigh phase, I'm afraid. I keep telling myself I'll leave a polite note but then I never get around to writing it.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Write the note. A friendly one works better than you'd think, people usually have no idea how much sound carries.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: You're right, I'll do it tonight. Anyway, did you get the invitation to Marit's wedding? Ours came on Friday.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Yes! It's such a lovely card, all handwritten. I can't believe she's actually getting married, I still picture her as the person who lost her shoes at that festival.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Right, she walked home barefoot and was weirdly proud of it. Are you going to make a weekend of it or just do the day?

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: I was thinking of staying over, since it's a bit of a drive. Do you want to share a ride when it gets closer?

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Sure, that would be fun, and it means neither of us has to be the sober one driving back late.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Exactly my thinking. We can sort out the details nearer the time, there's plenty of runway.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Perfect. I'm going to go write that note to the neighbour before I lose my nerve, talk soon!

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Good luck with it! Tell me how it goes, and I'll send you a photo of the muddy boots for the record.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Hey you! How's the week looking so far? I feel like I haven't heard from you in ages.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Busy but good! I finally booked a checkup with Dr. Abernathy, so that's one thing ticked off the list.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Look at you being responsible. I've been putting mine off for a year at least.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Honestly the big news is that I've moved. I'm in Dunedin now, still unpacking boxes.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: No way, you buried the lede! How's it been settling in? Are the boxes winning?

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: They're winning by a mile. Slowly getting there though, and I bought myself a new plant to make the place feel less bare. It's the monstera, and it already looks great by the window.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Nice, those things get huge. Just don't let it take over the whole flat.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Ha, I'll hold it to a strict growth plan. Did you hear that Marit's wedding is finally locked in? I got the invite last week.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: I did! Mine came too. I'm already stressing about what to wear and whether I'll cry during the vows.

turns.speaker: Sunniva

turns.text: Hey you! Survived the week? I feel like August just evaporated.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Barely, ha. It's been one of those stretches where every day blurs into the next. How are you?

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Pretty good. I've been hooked on this podcast about lost expeditions, the kind where people vanish in the arctic and you just keep listening for 'one more episode'.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Oh that sounds exactly my thing. Is it narrated or more of an interview format?

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Narrated, with a guy who has this very calm voice that makes everything sound ominous. I fell asleep to it twice and then had to go back and find where I'd drifted off.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: That's the real test of a good podcast, honestly. Send me the name and I'll start it this weekend.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Will do. Oh, and I tried making a mushroom risotto on Sunday and it was a disaster. I got impatient and cranked the heat, so the rice was crunchy in the middle and burnt on the bottom.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Oh no, risotto punishes impatience. You really do have to stand there stirring and adding stock little by little.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: I know, I know. I ended up eating toast with cheese over the sink like a raccoon.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Honestly a respectable dinner. I've had worse ones that were supposedly planned.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Did you get outside at all this month? I finally did a proper hike last weekend, the ridge trail with the long climb through the pines.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Nice! Was the view worth it? I always say the last twenty minutes of a climb are where you question every life choice.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Completely worth it. The whole valley was lit up and there was hardly anyone else on the trail. My knees complained the entire way down though.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Knees always send the bill the next day. I'd love to try that trail sometime, it sounds like my kind of quiet.

turns.speaker: Teodor
turns.text: Let's do it in September when it's cooler. I'll bring snacks and you can bring the podcast recommendations you owe me.

turns.speaker: Sunniva
turns.text: Deal. I'll start yours tonight and report back, and you promise to skip the risotto.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Hey Kwame, how's your Monday going so far?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Not bad. I finally got the new laptop set up over the weekend, and it's so much faster that I keep opening things just to watch them load.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, nice. Mine is still the old one and it sounds like a small jet whenever I join a video call.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Put in a request, they were pretty quick about mine. The migration of my dotfiles was the only annoying part.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Good to know. Did you try the coffee machine on the second floor yet? Someone apparently fixed it.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I did, and it's a big improvement. Before it tasted like warm cardboard, now it's actually drinkable, which is dangerous for my caffeine habits.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Dangerous for the rest of us too, there was a queue this morning. Anyway, anything I should know about before the week gets going?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Just that I'm on the on-call rotation starting this week, so if I look a bit tired later, that's why.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Oh, good luck with that. I hope your phone stays quiet at night.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Me too. Also, heads up, a new blocker bug was opened on the release this morning: the broken password reset.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Okay, thanks for flagging it. I'll make sure it gets looked at first thing tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Sounds good. I'm also fighting a flaky test that passes on my machine and then randomly fails when run with the rest of the suite.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Those are the worst. Is it a timing thing, or does it only fail in certain orders?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Probably timing, but I haven't proven it yet. I'll poke at it after lunch with the new laptop, at least it'll fail faster now.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, small wins. Ping me if you want a second pair of eyes on it.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Will do. Enjoy the rest of your Monday, and go grab some of that coffee before the queue gets long again.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Hey Kwame, how's your week going? Mine's been all meetings so far, I'm barely surviving.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Not bad at all. Yesterday's team lunch was the highlight, we finally tried that Ethiopian place near the office.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Oh nice, I heard about that. I had to skip it for a call, which still stings a little. Was it good?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Really good. The injera was great and everyone shared off big platters, so it got pretty chatty. Even the quiet folks opened up.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: That's the best kind of lunch. Speaking of quiet folks, how's the new hire settling in? I've only caught glimpses of them in standup.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Doing well, I think. They've been asking a lot of questions, which I like. Yesterday they asked where a certain setup step was written down and I had to admit it lives mostly in my head.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, that's the documentation debt talking. I keep meaning to block off time for it and then something else eats the calendar.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Same here. Honestly the newcomer is doing us a favor, every question they ask shows a gap we've stopped noticing.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: That's a good way to look at it. Maybe we have them jot down every spot where they got stuck and turn it into proper docs.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I like that. Fresh eyes write better onboarding notes than any of us would, since we skip all the steps we do on autopilot.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Exactly. And it gives them an early win too, they get to leave a mark without touching anything risky.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Yeah, I'll suggest it at the start of next week. I'll pair with them for the first pass so it doesn't feel like homework.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Perfect. If it goes well we could try the same trick on the older pages nobody's touched in ages.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Some of those are fossils at this point. Half of them describe things we stopped doing ages ago.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, archaeology by wiki. Okay, I should run to my next meeting, but this was a nice break.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Go, go. Talk in a couple of weeks, and say hi to the newcomer when you bump into them.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Hey Kwame, how's the week treating you? Feels like it's been a long one over here.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Pretty good actually, just quiet. The new person on the team started Monday and I've been showing them around the codebase.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Oh nice, how are they settling in? I only caught them briefly in the hallway on Tuesday.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Really well. Asks good questions, doesn't pretend to understand things when they don't. That's rarer than you'd think.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Love that. Honestly the best thing about onboarding someone is how it exposes everything we never wrote down.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Ha, yes. Half of what I explained on Monday was just stuff living in my head. I kept saying 'oh, it's sort of tribal knowledge' and then feeling guilty.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Documentation debt is real. We keep promising ourselves a cleanup sprint and then something shinier shows up.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I started a rough getting-started page just from the questions they asked. Nothing polished, but it's already better than what we had.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: That's honestly the perfect way to do it. Write down what a real person actually needed, not what you imagine they'd need.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Exactly. If I'd tried to write it in the abstract I'd still be staring at an empty page.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Maybe we could all chip in a little each week. Even ten minutes after standup would add up.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I'd be up for that. Small and regular beats a big heroic push that never happens.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Speaking of the new person, we should do a team lunch next week so they can meet everyone properly. Nothing fancy.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Yes please. There's that noodle place around the corner that's easy for a big group, and they do decent vegetarian stuff too.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Perfect, I'll float it in the team channel and see what day works for most people.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Sounds good. Thursday tends to be the calmest day for me, but I'm flexible.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Noted, I'll lean toward Thursday. Okay, I'll let you get back to it. Enjoy the quiet while it lasts!

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Hey Kwame, how's your week going? Feels like it's been one of those where everything takes twice as long.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Ha, yes, exactly that. I lost most of Tuesday chasing a flaky test that passed on my machine ten times in a row and then failed on the first run after lunch.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ugh, the worst kind. Did you figure out what was going on?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Pretty sure it's a timing thing, something racing with something else. I put a retry around it for now so it stops bothering everyone, but I don't love it.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: A retry is fine as a bandage as long as we don't forget it's there. Maybe leave a comment so future-you knows to come back to it?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Already did, with a very passive-aggressive comment too. Anyway, are you coming to the team lunch on Friday?

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Yes! I voted for the noodle place. Last time we went somewhere with a ninety-minute wait and I nearly gave up.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Noodles get my vote too. I'll be there as long as nothing catches fire before noon.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Knock on wood. Oh, did your laptop upgrade ever come through? You were complaining about the fans a while back.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: It showed up on Wednesday! I spent half a day moving everything over, but the thing is silent now. Builds that used to make my desk vibrate don't even wake it up.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Nice, I'm a little jealous. Mine's still holding on, but the battery gives up around two in the afternoon.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: You should put in a request. IT was pretty quick about mine once I sent the right form.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Maybe I will. I keep telling myself I'll do it after the next release, which is basically never.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Ha, that's how I put mine off for a year. Just do it now and thank yourself later.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Fine, you've convinced me. I'll fill it out after lunch today.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Good. And save me a seat at the noodle place on Friday, I'll bring my quiet laptop as a trophy.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Hey Kwame, got a few minutes? I wanted to ask how code review has been feeling lately, since a couple of people mentioned some comments getting a bit sharp.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Sure, I've got time. I think it's mostly a tone thing, people write terse comments when they're rushed and it lands harder than intended.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: That makes sense. Do you have a rule of thumb you follow when you're leaving feedback?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I try to phrase things as questions first, like 'what happens if this is null?' instead of 'this is wrong.' And I always say something good about the change before I pile on the nitpicks.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: I like that. Maybe we could put a short note about it in the contributor guide so newer folks see it from the start.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Good idea. And speaking of the contributor guide, anyone cloning the code should know it lives in a repository named kestrel-core, since I keep seeing people ask in chat where to find it.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, yes, I'll make sure that's at the top of the guide. Which brings me to documentation, honestly we have so much debt there it's a bit embarrassing.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Agreed. Half the setup steps in the wiki are out of date, and nobody wants to be the one to rewrite them.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: What if we carve out an hour at the end of each sprint just for docs? Nothing fancy, just fixing whatever tripped someone up that week.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I'd be up for that. Small and regular beats a giant cleanup that never gets scheduled.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Exactly. Oh, on a different note, did you end up watching that conference talk I sent you last week?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I did, the one about designing for failure? I thought the speaker was great, especially the bit about writing runbooks before you actually need them.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Right, that was my favorite part too. It kind of ties back to the docs conversation, doesn't it?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: It really does. Maybe our docs hour can start with a runbook or two.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Perfect, I'll put it on the agenda for the next planning session. Thanks for the chat, Kwame.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Anytime, talk soon!

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Hey Kwame, are you coming to the team lunch on Thursday? I'm trying to get a rough headcount before I book the table.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Yep, count me in. Is it the Thai place again or are we trying somewhere new?

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Somewhere new, a little noodle spot near the station. Apparently the portions are huge, so come hungry.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Perfect, I skipped breakfast on purpose then. Also, quick tangent: I just spent twenty minutes waiting on a pipeline run, and it reminded me that everything we ship goes through TeamCity, so those queues really do shape my mornings.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, so that's where all your coffee breaks come from. Speaking of which, the office coffee machine is making that grinding noise again.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: It sounds like it's chewing gravel. I think someone keeps putting the oily beans in it.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Probably me, guilty. I'll stick to the normal ones from now on and leave a note on the lid.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: A note might actually work, people respect a sticky note more than you'd think.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Random question while we're chatting: how do you feel about the tone of code review comments lately? I overheard someone say a comment felt a bit blunt.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I think most of us mean well, but text strips out tone. I try to phrase things as questions, like 'what do you think about trying X here?' instead of just saying it's wrong.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: That's a good habit. I'd love it if more people also said something nice before the nitpicks.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Agreed, even a quick 'nice cleanup' goes a long way. I'll mention it at the next team sync, nothing heavy-handed.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Great, that would help a lot. Okay, I'll go finalize the lunch booking and bring a gentle reminder about the coffee beans.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Sounds good. See you Thursday, and save me a seat near the noodles.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Hey Kwame, are you coming to the team lunch on Friday? I'm trying to get a headcount to the restaurant before they close bookings.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Yes, count me in. Is it the Thai place again or did someone finally talk everyone into trying the new ramen spot?

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ramen won, narrowly. Mostly because Dara threatened to skip lunch entirely if we went Thai a third time.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Fair enough, that's a legitimate threat. I'll bring my appetite and an open mind.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Perfect. Oh, and while I have you, I've been staring at our docs folder and it's embarrassing. Half the pages haven't been touched in ages.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Yeah, documentation debt is real. I've got a couple of setup guides that I know are out of date because I keep fixing things in my head instead of on the page.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Same energy as me with the meeting notes. What if we set aside an hour every Friday afternoon, just for docs, nobody allowed to do anything else?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I like it in theory. In practice someone will get pulled into a fire and the hour will quietly vanish, but let's try it for a month and see.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Deal. I'll put a recurring block on everyone's calendar and call it something friendly so it doesn't feel like homework.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Call it 'tidy up time'. People respond to that better than 'documentation hour'.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, tidy up time it is. By the way, did you ever hear back about that conference talk you submitted?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I did, they accepted it! It's a short slot, twenty minutes, on lessons from running a small team's services in production.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: That's great news, congratulations! Are you nervous or are you the type who just wings it?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: A bit of both honestly. I'll write it all out, then ignore half of it on stage like I always do.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Run it past me beforehand if you want a practice audience. I'm happy to sit through it and heckle gently.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Gentle heckling is exactly what I need. I'll send you a draft once I've got slides that don't look like a wall of text.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Morning! How was your weekend, did you get any time offline?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Mostly, yeah. Took the bike out on Saturday and then did absolutely nothing on Sunday, which was great.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Sounds perfect. Anything I should know about before the week kicks off?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: One thing, a new blocker bug got opened on the release this morning: the login timeout. Sessions are dropping way earlier than they should.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ugh, okay. Is someone already looking at it or should I rearrange things?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I'll take a first pass today. I'll let you know if it needs more hands.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Thanks. Also, that flaky test is back again, the one that fails maybe one run in ten. Drives me nuts.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Yeah, I've seen it. It's probably a timing thing, I'll try to pin it down rather than just rerunning it forever.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Please do. Rerunning until green feels like cheating.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Totally. Speaking of things we keep putting off, the docs are in rough shape. Half of the setup notes are out of date.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: I know, documentation debt is real. I'll try to carve out a half day for it next sprint, maybe we all chip in.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: That'd help. Honestly the people who care most about it are the ones onboarding new folks, and they're always the first to complain.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Fair. Oh, and I should say the client demo prep is going to eat some of my week, so I might be slow to reply.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: No worries. Everything we do is for Northwind Dairy anyway, so I get why that takes priority.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Exactly. Hey, are you coming to the team lunch on Thursday? I think we're trying that new noodle place.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Definitely, I'm in. I'll be the one ordering way too much.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Morning Liesel. That flaky test is back again, it failed twice overnight and then passed on a rerun with no changes.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ugh, those are the worst. Is it the same one as before or a new troublemaker?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Same one, I think. Timing issue most likely, I'll poke at it this afternoon. Oh, and for the architecture doc, the database the Kestrel project uses is PostgreSQL, so I'm writing the schema notes with that in mind.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Perfect, thanks. Also I'm trying to tidy up the ownership list for the wiki, who's looking after billing these days?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: The billing module is owned by Leilani now, she's been all over it for a while.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Great, I'll put her name down. Are we still doing the team lunch on Friday? I need to book somewhere.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Yes please, I'm in. Somewhere with decent vegetarian options would be great, a couple of people asked.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Easy enough. Before I forget, I need the budget figure for the finance review.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Sure, our quarterly cloud budget is $18,000, and we're sitting comfortably under that so far.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Good to hear. And where are we hosting the service again? Finance asks about that too.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: It's hosted in Mumbai.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Wait, sorry, that was a mistake. It's not Mumbai, it's Oregon. I mixed it up with another project.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: No worries, I'll write that down properly this time. Did your laptop upgrade ever come through?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Finally, yes! The new one arrived Tuesday and builds are so much faster, I almost don't have time to get coffee anymore.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, the dream. Anything else I should know before the planning meeting?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Two things. We have a contract with the vendor Quillon for load testing, so you can mention that to the stakeholders.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: And a new blocker bug was opened on the release: the sync memory leak. I'll dig into it after the flaky test.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Thanks for the heads up, I'll flag it in the meeting. Talk in a couple of weeks!
