turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Morning! How's the week treating you? Did the new person on the team find their feet yet?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Pretty well, I think. They've stopped asking where the coffee machine is, which I count as a milestone.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, that's the real onboarding checklist. I told them to grab me anytime if they get stuck on anything.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Good. Oh, before I forget, we moved off what we had before, and Kestrel now runs on MariaDB. Migration went through without much drama.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Nice, that's a relief. I was braced for a weekend of firefighting.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Me too. By the way, my new laptop finally arrived. The old one sounded like a jet engine every time I compiled anything.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Lucky you! Mine is due for a refresh too, but I keep putting off the hassle of setting everything up again. Also, heads up, Odalys is the one who owns the billing module now, so route any questions there.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Got it, I'll point people her way. The setup is honestly not bad, I just cloned my dotfiles and was mostly running in an hour.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: That's encouraging. Maybe I'll stop procrastinating then.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Also, I need to fix something I told you earlier. The quarterly cloud budget isn't $18,000, that was my mistake. It's $24,500.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Okay, thanks for catching that. I'll update my notes so I don't repeat the wrong figure to anyone.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Appreciate it. I'm also chasing a flaky test right now, one of those that passes five times and then fails on the sixth for no reason.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Those are the worst. Is it a timing thing, or does it look random?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Feels like timing, but I haven't pinned it down yet. Anyway, a new blocker got opened on the release this morning: the timezone drift.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ugh, okay. Let's talk about it in the next sync and figure out who can look at it first.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Sounds good. I'll write up what I know before then so we're not starting cold.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Morning! How's your Monday going so far?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Not bad. Finally got the new laptop set up over the weekend, and the difference in build times is kind of ridiculous.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, nice. Did you have to reinstall everything from scratch or did the migration tool do its job?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Mostly the tool, but I still spent an hour chasing down my editor settings. Anyway, quick heads up for you, billing is Priya's now, so any questions on that go to her.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Good to know, I'll update my notes. Is she comfortable picking it up?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Yeah, she's been reading through it all week. She left a few thoughtful comments on my last pull request too.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Speaking of reviews, I keep meaning to ask whether people are being kind enough in them. I saw one comment last week that was a bit blunt.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I think most folks are fine. My rule is to ask a question instead of making a demand, and to say what's good before what's not.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: That's a good rule. Maybe we should write that down somewhere for newer people.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: We could, but then it joins the pile of docs we never finish. Our documentation debt is honestly embarrassing at this point.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Don't remind me. I looked at the onboarding page yesterday and half the screenshots are from two versions ago.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Right, and for anything about how the UI should look, just talk to Anselm, he leads design on the project. He's the one who actually knows why things are the way they are.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Makes sense, I'll grab some time with him. Maybe he can help me fix those screenshots too.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Oh, and one more thing before I forget: a new blocker got opened on the release, the duplicate invoice bug.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ugh, okay. Thanks for flagging it, I'll look at it first thing after lunch.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Sounds good. Talk in a couple of weeks, or sooner if something blows up.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Morning! Did the new laptop finally show up? You were complaining about the old one last time.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: It did, it arrived Tuesday. The fans don't sound like a jet engine anymore, which is honestly the main upgrade for me.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, worth every penny then. Did the migration of your setup go okay?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Mostly. Dotfiles came over fine, but I spent an hour fixing my terminal font. Also the pipeline reran clean on it, which is nice now that we build on CircleCI, so I could check everything worked end to end.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Good, that's the kind of boring success I like. Speaking of boring successes, anything I should know before the status update?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: One thing, yes. The blocker the login timeout was fixed and closed, so that's off the list for good.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Great, I'll mention it in the update. Thanks for chasing that down.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Sure thing. Unrelated, but I got a comment on my pull request yesterday that was just 'this is wrong.' No explanation, nothing.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Oof. That's rough. I always think a review comment should say what's wrong and ideally suggest a direction.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Exactly. I try to start with what I liked before I get to the nitpicks, even if it's small. It changes how people take the rest.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Agreed. Tone matters more than people think, especially in writing where there's no face to soften it.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Totally. Anyway, did you get to watch any of the conference talks you bookmarked?

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: One of them, the keynote on running small teams well. Lots of good stuff, though the speaker clicked through slides way too fast.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I've been thinking of submitting a talk of my own next year. Something practical, like lessons from untangling messy code.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: You should! People love war stories, and you tell them well. I'd happily be your test audience.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Deal. I'll draft an outline and send it your way, fair warning that it'll be rough.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Rough is fine. Talk soon, and enjoy the quiet fans!

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Hey Kwame! How's your Monday going so far?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Pretty decent, just got back from lunch. I've been meaning to tell you, I watched that conference talk everyone's been raving about, the one on writing docs people actually read.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Oh nice, was it worth the hour? I keep seeing clips of it in my feed.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Totally worth it. The speaker basically said documentation debt compounds like financial debt, and that hit a little too close to home.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, tell me about it. Our wiki has pages that haven't been touched in ages, and half of them describe things we don't even do anymore.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Right? Speaking of things that moved, we're on MySQL for Kestrel now, so a few of those old pages are definitely wrong.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Good to know, I'll flag that when I do my next pass through the wiki. Maybe I'll block out a Friday afternoon just for cleanup.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Do it, and bribe people with snacks. Nobody volunteers for docs unless there's food involved.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Cookies it is. Oh, and I finally got approval for a laptop upgrade, mine has been wheezing every time I open more than three tabs.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Finally! Do you know what you're getting, or is IT picking for you?

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: I get to choose from a short list. I'm leaning toward the lighter one, since I carry it everywhere and my shoulder has opinions.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Go light. I went the other way with mine last time, big screen and heavy as a brick, and I regret it every time I travel.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Noted, no bricks. Did you at least enjoy the rest of the conference talks?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: A couple were good. The docs one was the standout though, I might even try the template idea the speaker showed for new pages.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Send me the link when you get a chance, I'd like to watch it over lunch this week.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Will do, I'll drop it in our chat in a minute. Talk in a couple of weeks!

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Hey Kwame, how's the week going? I saw you were at that conference talk on Tuesday, was it any good?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: It was decent actually. The speaker covered how to keep code reviews from turning into arguments, and honestly I took a few notes for myself.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, we could all use that. What was the main takeaway?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Mostly just phrase things as questions instead of orders. 'What do you think about extracting this?' lands way better than 'extract this.'

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Fair point. Oh, before I forget, Henrik is the one who owns the billing module now, so route any questions there to him.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Got it, I'll ping him next time something comes up. Is he already up to speed on it?

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Getting there. He's been reading through it all week, and he's a quick study.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Good. Speaking of reading, I've been trying to chip away at our documentation debt. Half the setup notes are stale and nobody trusts them.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Yeah, that's been nagging at me too. Greta leads design on the project and has been all along, and even she told me she can't find the current component guidelines anywhere.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I started a little pass on the onboarding doc yesterday. Mostly deleting things that are flat-out wrong, which is oddly satisfying.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Deleting wrong docs is underrated. Better a short true page than a long misleading one.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Exactly. Also, small news on my end: I got taken off the on-call rotation, so my nights should be a lot calmer now.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, your sleep schedule thanks you. Enjoy it.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Oh and good news from the engineering side too: the sync memory leak got fixed and closed this morning, so that one's finally off the list.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Wonderful, that's a relief. Thanks for chasing it down.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: No problem. Want to do a docs sprint for an afternoon sometime? Pizza, headphones, lots of deleting.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Sold. Let me find a slot that works and I'll send an invite.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Hey Liesel, how's your Saturday going? I'm supposed to be relaxing but I keep thinking about the team lunch we had Thursday.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, same. That place was a good pick, I think everyone left happy. Even the people who usually skip lunch showed up.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Yeah, the long table helped. Nobody got stuck at the awkward end for once.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: True. Maybe we should do it monthly, rotate who picks the spot.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I'd go for that. Though I'd get nervous picking, I have no idea what the vegetarians on the team actually like.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Just ask in the channel, people love to have opinions about food. It's the one topic where everyone's an expert.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Fair point. Oh, by the way, I've been meaning to ask what you think about code review manners. I left a pretty blunt comment on someone's PR this week and then felt weird about it.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Blunt how? Like rude, or just direct?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Direct, I thought. I wrote 'this function does too much, split it.' But reading it back, it's a bit curt with no context.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: I'd soften it a little, maybe add why splitting helps. People take written comments harder than you mean them, especially from someone senior.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Yeah, that's what I figured. I'll go back and add a line about testability so it reads like a suggestion instead of an order.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Good. Also a quick 'nice work on the rest' never hurts. It costs nothing and people remember it.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Agreed. How's the newcomer settling in, by the way? I haven't had a proper chat with them since they started.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Pretty well, I think. They're quiet in meetings but asked me some sharp questions one-on-one, so I think they're just taking it all in.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: That's a good sign. I'll invite them along next time I grab coffee, no pressure.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: They'd like that. Okay, I'm going to go enjoy what's left of the weekend, talk in a couple of weeks!

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Morning Liesel. Did you see the coffee machine finally got descaled? Tastes like actual coffee again instead of warm regret.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: I did! Someone taped a little note on it too, which I think was aimed at whoever keeps leaving it empty.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Guilty on at least two of those mornings. I'll start refilling the water, promise.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Ha, I'll hold you to that. Hey, did you catch any of the talks from that conference last week? I saw people posting about one on incremental refactoring.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: I watched the recording of that one, actually. The speaker's main point was that you should refactor in tiny steps alongside feature work rather than booking a giant cleanup sprint that never happens.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: That sounds painfully relevant. Our giant cleanup sprint has been 'next quarter' for as long as I can remember.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Right? Same energy as our documentation, honestly. We have a lot of pages that describe how things worked about a year ago.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Documentation debt is the one I feel guilty about most. Half the onboarding guide references steps nobody does anymore.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: What if we tried the talk's approach there too? Whoever touches a part of the system fixes the related doc page in the same change, no separate project.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: I like that. It's small enough that people might actually do it. I could add a line to the review checklist so it's a habit.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: That would help a lot. Reviewers tend to follow whatever's on the checklist, so it'd stick better than a reminder in chat.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Okay, I'll draft it this afternoon and send it around for feedback. Did the speaker say anything about measuring whether it works?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Sort of. Just tracking how often people say 'the docs were wrong' in standup, which is a very unscientific but weirdly effective metric.

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: I love that. Free, easy, and we'd know quickly if it's helping.

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Agreed. Anyway, I'm going to go refill that coffee machine before I forget. Want a cup?

turns.speaker: Liesel
turns.text: Yes please, strong as it'll go. Thanks Kwame!

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Hi Rafiq, hope your week's off to a decent start. Did the office close for the long weekend like you thought it might?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: It did, yes, we were shut Monday and I actually stayed away from my laptop for once. Feels like I'm paying for it today though, my inbox is a mess.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Ha, that's always the way. Is it busy generally at the moment?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Properly busy, yes. Three other clients all want things turned around by Friday, so I'm juggling a bit. Nothing I can't handle, but I'll be a little slower replying than usual this week.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: No worries at all, I'm not in a rush this week. I'd rather you get it right than get it fast.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Appreciate that. Speaking of getting it right, I spotted a silly typo in the latest draft when I was reading it over this morning.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Oh no, what was it? Something embarrassing?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Just a doubled word and a company name with a letter missing. Harmless, but I'd have hated for it to go out like that.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Better you caught it than me. I read that thing three times and my eyes just slide over mistakes by now.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Same here, honestly. I find the only trick is printing it out or changing the font, then the errors suddenly jump out.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: That's a good tip, I'll try that. Did you do anything nice with your day off, by the way?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Mostly cooked and watched a film I'd been putting off for ages. Very low key, which was exactly what I needed.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Sounds perfect. We were closed too, so I caught up on sleep and not much else.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Sleep is underrated. Anyway, I'll send over the corrected draft once I've fixed that typo and had another proper read.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Great, thanks. No hurry, like I said.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Will do. Speak in a couple of weeks, and shout if anything comes up before then.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Morning Rafiq! I read through the latest draft over the weekend and spotted a typo on page 4, "supplyer" with a y. Tiny thing but it jumped out at me.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, good catch. I'll fix that in the next turn of the document, I'm amazed it survived three read-throughs.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Honestly I only noticed because I was reading it on the train with nothing else to do.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Whatever works! Anyway, I wanted to tell you where we landed with the other side on the cap. They've agreed the liability cap is $5 million, so that's settled from my point of view.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Oh nice, that's a relief. I wasn't sure they'd move at all on that one.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: They took a while to come round, but we got there. Speaking of which, they're being painfully slow to reply at the moment. I sent my last email nine days ago and only got an answer this morning.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Nine days? That's ridiculous. Do you think they're doing it on purpose to wear us down?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Hard to say. Could be tactics, could just be that their people are swamped. I'd lean towards disorganised rather than devious.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Fair enough. Oh, one thing I meant to mention, when I spoke to our ops team they raised a new point they want covered, the delivery penalties. They think we need something clear in there.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Okay, thanks for flagging it. Let me think about how best to frame that and I'll come back to you with a suggestion.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Sounds good, no rush. I know you've got a lot on.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Not too bad this week, though the office is closed on Friday for the holiday, so I'll be offline that day.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Lucky you, a long weekend! I think we're open but half the team has booked it off anyway.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, classic. I'll aim to get the corrected draft over to you before I log off Thursday, typo included.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Perfect, thanks Rafiq. Talk in a couple of weeks!

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Hi Rafiq, hope your weekend was decent. I spent most of Friday walking a visitor round the plant and my feet are still complaining.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, mine was quiet, thanks. How did the visit go? Anyone get lost among the machines?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Nobody got lost, but the guy kept stopping to ask about every single conveyor. Took us twice as long as planned.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Classic. At least he was interested. Better than someone checking their phone the whole time.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: True. Anyway, on the agreement, I want to nail one thing down so we stop going round in circles: the minimum annual order volume is 55,000 units. That's settled on our side.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Understood, I'll treat that as fixed and work from it in the next draft.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Speaking of the draft, I found a typo in the version I sent you last week. Someone's name was spelled two different ways in the same paragraph, which is embarrassing.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Ha, I didn't even notice. I probably read it too fast on the train.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: No harm done, I've already corrected it. I'll send a clean copy later today.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Great. Oh, and something new popped up on their side this week: the insurance certificates. They've started asking about them and I wasn't expecting that.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Okay, thanks for flagging it. Can you forward whatever they sent you so I can see exactly what they're asking for?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Will do this afternoon. Honestly, I'd have sent it sooner but it took them ages to even get back to me about it.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Yes, they've been slow with me too. I sent a short question on Tuesday and I'm still waiting.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Typical. Do you want me to nudge them from my end, or would that just annoy them?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: A friendly nudge from you can't hurt. I'll chase on my side tomorrow if we've heard nothing.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Sounds good. Talk in a couple of weeks, or sooner if they surprise us and actually reply.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Hi Rafiq, hope your week's going alright. I was at the plant most of yesterday walking some visitors round, and my feet are still complaining.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, sounds like a long day. Did the visit go well, or was it one of those where everything breaks the minute guests arrive?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Pretty smooth, actually. One of the machines made a horrible noise right as we passed it, but nobody seemed to mind.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Classic. Machines always know when there's an audience.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Anyway, on the deal itself, a new one came up this week that I wanted to flag. The other side raised the indemnity wording and said they want to rework it.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Okay, thanks for telling me. I'll take a look at what they've sent and think about how we want to respond.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Great. And speaking of the other side, they take forever to get back to us. I sent a quick question on Monday and I'm still waiting.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Yes, I've noticed the same. Their replies tend to trickle in two or three days late, so I've stopped expecting anything quick.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: At least there's some good news too. We finally got the delivery penalties settled, which feels like a weight off.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: That's a relief, that one was dragging on. I'll update the draft so it reflects what you agreed.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Perfect. By the way, I spotted a typo in the latest draft you sent. There's a word in one clause that's missing a letter and it changes the meaning a bit.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Oh no, thanks for catching that. Which clause was it? I'd rather fix it before it goes any further.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: It's in the middle section, I'll send you a screenshot so you can find it quickly.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Please do. I'll correct it and send round a clean version in the next day or so.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Sounds good. Thanks Rafiq, talk in a couple of weeks unless something comes up.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Will do. Enjoy the rest of your week, and give your feet a rest!

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Hi Rafiq, hope your week is going okay. Are you around the Easter break at all?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Hi Ottilie, doing well thanks. The office closes from Thursday through the Monday after, so I'll be offline for a few days. I'll flag anything urgent before I go.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Fair enough, you deserve the rest. Our plant shuts for that stretch too, so it works out nicely.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Good. Speaking of the plant, didn't you have a visit lined up there recently?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Yes, the Marlow team came by last week and walked the whole floor. They seemed genuinely impressed with the line, and the engineers got along well.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: That's encouraging. Site visits like that tend to smooth things along. Did they ask many questions?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Loads, mostly practical stuff. Oh, and while I remember, we've settled that deliveries go to Bilbao, so please make sure that's what the draft says.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Noted, I'll check the draft against that and correct it if needed. Thanks for catching it.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: No problem. Honestly the bigger frustration is how slow they are to reply. I sent a question ten days ago and heard nothing until yesterday.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Yes, I've noticed the same on my end. Their side tends to go quiet for a week and then fire back several answers at once.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Exactly that. Is it worth nudging them a bit more firmly, or would that just annoy them?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: A polite but firm nudge with a clear deadline usually works. I can draft something short for you to send under your name if you like.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Please do. Also, one thing I wanted to make sure we're aligned on: the agreement includes an exclusivity clause, right?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Understood, I'll keep that in view as I go through the draft. I'll send you the nudge email tomorrow so you can have it out before the break.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Perfect, thank you. Enjoy the long weekend when it comes.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: You too, Ottilie. Talk in a couple of weeks.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Hi Rafiq, hope your week is going okay. I just got back from walking the plant floor with some visitors and my feet are done.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Hi Ottilie! Mine's been a bit of a blur, honestly. How did the visit go?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Pretty well. The guys were impressed with the new packing line, and nobody tripped over anything, which I count as a win.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, low bar but a good one. I always worry when I visit a factory that I'll wander into the wrong yellow line.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: You'd be fine, we'd give you a hi-vis vest and a stern look. Anyway, while I have you, I should mention that Ms. Oyelaran is the one who'll be signing for Marlow Ltd.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Good to know, thanks for passing that along. I'll keep that in mind as we go.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: No problem. Have you heard anything back from their side lately? I feel like I've been waiting forever.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Nothing yet, sadly. They're not exactly speedy, every reply seems to take them days.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: It's maddening. I send one email and then just stare at my inbox like it owes me money.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, I know that feeling. I've started batching my chasers so I'm not pestering them every other day.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Smart. How's your workload, by the way? You sound like you're juggling a lot.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: It's been heavy. Three other matters landed on my desk at once this week, so I've been living on coffee.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Oof, please don't burn out on me. I need you sharp.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, I'll do my best. I'm planning a quiet weekend to recover, maybe just a long walk and a lot of nothing.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: That sounds perfect. I might do the same once this plant visit stuff settles down.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Sounds like a plan. Talk again in a couple of weeks, and enjoy putting your feet up tonight.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Morning Ottilie. How did the visit to your plant go last week? You said you had the whole afternoon booked.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Morning! It went well, though it ran long. I ended up walking the floor with the production team for nearly four hours and my feet are still complaining.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, that's the price of actually going and looking. Did anything useful come out of it?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Quite a bit. The line supervisor showed me how they handle changeovers, which I'd never really understood from the reports. Oh, and speaking of the deal, Marlow came back to us yesterday and raised something new: the tooling ownership.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Right, I wondered if that would surface. Can you forward me their email so I can read their exact wording before we talk about it?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Sure, I'll send it over after we're done chatting. It was only a short paragraph, nothing too elaborate.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Good. Short paragraphs sometimes hide the most inconvenient assumptions, so I'll read it carefully. By the way, I spotted a typo in the latest draft, a clause number that points to the wrong section.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Oh no, did I miss that when I read it? I went through it twice on the train.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Don't worry, it's an easy one to miss. It's a cross-reference that didn't update when we reshuffled the sections. I've already fixed it in my copy.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Thank you. Please send me the corrected version so I'm not working from the old one.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Will do, it'll be in your inbox this afternoon. Shall we pencil in the next call? I'm fairly open the week after next.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Let me check my diary. I'm travelling for the first half of that week, but Thursday looks free.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Thursday works for me. Mid-morning, say ten thirty, so you're not rushing from an early train?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Ten thirty is perfect. I'll put it in my calendar now.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Great, I'll send an invite too. Have a good rest of your Monday, and rest those feet.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Ha, I will. Speak soon, Rafiq.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Hi Rafiq, did you get a chance to look at the latest draft? I spotted a typo on the second page, our company name has an extra letter in it.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, good catch. I read that page three times and still missed it. I'll fix it in the next version.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: No worries, it's the sort of thing you only see when you're not staring at it all day. How's your week going, you sound busy?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Honestly it's been a bit of a crush. Three other matters landed on my desk at once, so I'm working through evenings. But yours is still near the top of the pile.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: I appreciate that. Still waiting on Marlow to get back to us on the last round, by the way. I sent a nudge to my contact there, and since the cargo is going into Felixstowe now I'm keen to get things moving, but nothing yet.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Yes, they've been slow every time. I chased their side again on Monday and got an automatic out-of-office back.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Typical. Do you think they're doing it on purpose, to wear us down?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Possibly, though I think it's more likely just internal sign-off dragging. Big companies tend to move at the pace of their slowest approver.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: That makes sense. I'd rather they were slow than difficult, I suppose.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Fair point. Slow is annoying but manageable. I'll send them a polite reminder tomorrow and copy you in.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Perfect, thank you. Do you want me to proofread the next draft before it goes out? A second pair of eyes might help with the typos.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: That would actually be really useful, given how my eyes are feeling this week. I'll send it over once I've made the fixes.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Sounds good. Try to get some rest in between all those matters, won't you?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: I'll do my best. A long weekend is coming up and I'm planning to do absolutely nothing.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Sounds lovely. Speak in a couple of weeks, or sooner if Marlow finally wakes up.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Will do. Talk soon, Ottilie.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Hi Rafiq, hope your week is starting okay. Are you buried at the moment?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Pretty buried, honestly, but nothing I can't handle. Mondays are always a pile-up of emails.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: I hear you. One thing I wanted to pass on: the person signing for Marlow Ltd is now Ms. Devereux, so it's no longer the person we'd been expecting.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Okay, thanks for letting me know. I'll update the signature block on my side.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: I also wanted to tell you that the liability cap has moved to $1.2 million after the latest round of comments.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Got it, that's useful to know. Thanks for chasing that down.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Oh, and the agreement is governed by Ontario law, just so you have it for the cover page.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Wait, sorry, I need to take that back. It's not Ontario law, that was a mistake on my part. It's English law.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Good catch, glad you flagged it straight away. I'll make sure the draft reflects that.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Thanks. Now, for the printing, do you want me to print the signature pages at the office or would you rather send them over?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: I'll send a PDF set and you can print on your end. Just sign in blue ink if you can, it photocopies better.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Easy enough. Do I need a witness, or can I just sign and scan it back to you?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Just sign and scan for now, and we'll swap the originals by courier later.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Perfect. By the way, Marlow's lawyers are the firm Hartwell Breck, in case you want to loop them in on the signing logistics.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Will do, I'll reach out to them this week. When should we have our next call?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Two weeks from now works for me, mornings are best. Just send an invite and I'll accept it.
