turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Hi Rafiq, got a minute? I was reading through the latest draft last night and spotted a typo in the definitions section.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Of course. Which one? I read that draft twice and clearly my eyes glazed over somewhere.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: One of the defined terms is spelled two different ways, once with a double letter and once without. Tiny thing, but it jumped out at me.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Good catch, thank you. I'll fix it and check whether the same slip crept in anywhere else before we send the next version over.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Speaking of sending things over, have they come back to you on anything yet? I haven't heard a peep.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Not a word since last week. They're honestly the slowest people I've dealt with this year, every reply takes days.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: That's what I figured. I sent them a quick note myself on Monday and got nothing back, not even an acknowledgement.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Classic. I'll nudge them again tomorrow morning, politely, and see if that shakes anything loose.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Thanks. Oh, one thing I meant to mention while I think of it: there's an escrow arrangement for the tooling costs, so that's something to keep in mind when you're reading the drafts.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Noted, I'll keep that in view as I go through. How are you doing otherwise, is the rest of your week manageable?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Pretty hectic but fine. What about you, are you drowning in work at the moment?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: A bit, yes. I've got three other matters all landing deadlines at once, so I'm living on coffee and calendar reminders.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Ouch. Please don't burn out on my account, I'd rather you take an extra day than send me something rushed.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, I appreciate that. Don't worry, yours gets proper attention, it's just the evenings that suffer.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Fair enough. Let's catch up again in a couple of weeks unless something moves sooner.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Sounds good. I'll fix that typo and ping you the moment I hear anything back.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Hi Ottilie, good to hear from you. How was the visit to the plant?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Pretty good actually. Walked the whole line with the floor manager and the new packing area is finally running.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Nice, that must be a relief after all the delays. Did you get any time to look at the draft I sent?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: I did, on the train back. Quick check, the payment term in there is 90 days, right? That's what I remember us landing on.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Yes, that's what the draft says. I'll leave it as is.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Good. Oh, and one thing from their side came in yesterday: they want to raise the audit rights, so that's a fresh item on the table.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Hm, that's a bit annoying this late in the process. I'll want to see exactly what they're asking for before I react.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Same here. On the bright side, we did finally close out the tooling ownership, so that one's off the list.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Great, that was a sticky one, so I'm glad it's done. One less thing to fight over.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: How's your workload? You sounded swamped last time.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Still swamped, honestly. I've got three other deals closing this month, so I'm living on coffee.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Ha, sorry to add to the pile. The other side is taking forever to reply, which doesn't help either.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Tell me about it. I sent them a note a week ago and got an out-of-office, then silence.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Classic. Anyway, I keep reminding myself the whole thing is just a supply deal for ceramic bearings, it shouldn't be this painful.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, they never are as simple as they should be. I'll chase them again tomorrow and send you a summary once they answer.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Perfect, thanks Rafiq. Talk in a couple of weeks.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Morning Ottilie. Still no word from the other side since Monday, which is becoming typical. I swear they reply in geological time.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Ha, tell me about it. I stopped holding my breath weeks ago.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Wise. One thing did come through though: who signs for Marlow Ltd has changed and it's now Mr. Nakagawa. I'll update the signature block on our side.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Okay, good to know. Do I need to do anything on my end for that?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Nothing at all for now, I'll just make sure the draft reflects it. How did the plant visit go, by the way? You mentioned a tour was coming up.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: It was good, actually. Walked the whole floor with a couple of their engineers and the place was spotless. Noisy though, my ears were ringing by lunchtime.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Sounds like a proper working site. Did you get to see the production line running?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Yes, a full shift in progress. It was reassuring to see it up close rather than just in photos.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Always worth it. Oh, and I found a typo in the latest draft, a clause number was referenced wrong in the definitions section. Small thing, but I've flagged it.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Good catch. Speaking of mistakes, I need to correct something I told you earlier. The payment term in the agreement is not 90 days, that was my error. It is 45 days.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Thanks for flagging that, glad you caught it before it went anywhere. I'll make sure everything on my side matches.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Sorry about the mix-up. I think I had an old note in front of me.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: No harm done, it happens. I'd rather you tell me now than after a draft goes out.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Fair enough. Anything else you need from me this week?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Not really. I'll send over the corrected draft once I've fixed that typo, and then we wait for the other side to wake up.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Perfect. Talk in a couple of weeks, then. Enjoy the weekend!

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Hi Rafiq, any word from Marlow's side? I've been refreshing my inbox like a maniac.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Nothing yet. They took four days to answer a one-line question last week, so I'm not holding my breath.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Ugh, they're so slow. Though I did hear something useful through the grapevine: the person signing for Marlow Ltd is now Ms. Winterbourne.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Good to know, thanks. I'll make sure the signature block gets updated so we don't have to redo pages later.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Perfect. Oh, and the liability cap is now $3.5 million, in case that hadn't reached you yet.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Noted, I'll fold that into the next draft. Speaking of drafts, I spotted a typo in the one I sent you on Monday. A clause number was repeated twice.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Ha, I read that thing twice and missed it. Which section was it?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Near the end, in the boilerplate. Harmless, but I've already fixed it in the working copy.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Good catch. One more thing before I forget: the escrow arrangement was dropped.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Understood, I'll strip that out of the draft as well. Cleaner that way.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Now, signing logistics. Do you want me to print everything and sign in ink, or is a scanned signature fine?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Wet ink is safest for the main agreement, but scans are fine for the schedules. I can courier you the pages if you don't have a printer handy.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: I do have a printer, but it jams constantly. A courier sounds less stressful, honestly.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Done, I'll arrange it once the final version is ready. Use a blue pen so it's obvious which is the original.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Blue pen, got it. Talk in a couple of weeks, or sooner if Marlow ever wakes up!

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, I'll let you know the second they reply. Talk soon!

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Morning Rafiq! Hope your Saturday isn't entirely swallowed by work.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, mostly swallowed, but I've got coffee and a quiet office, so I can't complain.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: I was thinking the other day about that old deal we did together, the warehouse lease one. Remember how the landlord kept changing his mind about the car park?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: How could I forget. He rang me at 9pm on a Sunday about a single parking bay. I still bring it up as the gold standard of pointless drama.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: You handled it so calmly though. I'd have lost it.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Years of practice at looking calm while screaming inwardly. Speaking of which, I should say that our firm understanding is that the minimum annual order volume is 70,000 units, and that's what it's been all along.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Anyway, are you drowning at the moment? You sounded exhausted on the last call.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: A bit, yes. Three matters landed on my desk at once and one of them is a monster. But it's the good kind of busy, mostly.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Make sure you actually take a break at some point. Don't make me send you a wellness reminder.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Noted. I'm taking next Friday afternoon off, I swear. Not that anyone believes me.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: We should have you out to the plant sometime, by the way. You've never actually seen the production floor.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: I'd love that, honestly. I've only ever seen it in photos. Is it as noisy as everyone says?

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Louder. We hand out ear defenders at the door and the team has a whole system of hand signals.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Now I really want to come. I'll bring a hard hat and pretend I know what I'm looking at.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Deal. Maybe in a few weeks when things calm down. I'll check the calendar and message you.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Perfect. Enjoy what's left of your weekend, Ottilie.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Hi Rafiq, hope your week's not too manic. Feels like I haven't heard from you in ages, though I know that's not true.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, it's been a bit of a slog, honestly. I've got about four things all due before the end of the week and my inbox looks like a crime scene.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Oof, sorry to add to the pile. I'll keep this short then.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: No no, you're fine. Talking to you is the nice part of my day compared to some of the others.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Flattery. Are you at least getting a break soon? I seem to remember the office shuts for a bit.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Yes, we're closed on the Monday of the long weekend, so I'll be offline that day. I'm planning to do absolutely nothing and maybe fix the shed door.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: That sounds perfect. I might do the same, the shed is optional.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Strongly recommend the nothing part. The shed door is just guilt.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Speaking of waiting around, have you heard anything back from the other side lately?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Not yet. They took nearly a week to answer my last email, and when they did it was two lines saying they'd 'revert shortly'.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Shortly is doing a lot of work in that sentence.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Right? I've stopped checking for replies every hour. It's better for my blood pressure.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Wise. I'd rather you spend that energy on the shed door anyway.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Ha, don't tempt me. I'll nudge them again on Friday if we haven't heard anything.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Sounds good. Thanks for being so patient with all this.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Anytime. Talk in a couple of weeks, and enjoy the long weekend!

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Morning Rafiq. Still nothing back from Marlow, and it's been over a week now. Is it just me or are they getting slower?

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: It's not just you. They seem to take their time on everything lately, and a reply usually lands on a Friday afternoon when nobody can do anything with it.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Ha, classic. I keep refreshing my inbox like it's going to change anything.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: I did the same thing yesterday. Honestly I should stop, it's bad for my blood pressure.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Speaking of which, how's your workload? You sounded swamped last time we spoke.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Still pretty heavy. I've got three other clients all wanting things by the end of the month, so my desk looks like a paper explosion.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Sorry to add to the pile. I'll try to keep my emails short.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Oh, you're no trouble at all. You're one of the easier ones, you actually answer when I ask a question.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Low bar, but I'll take the compliment. By the way, I had some visitors at the plant on Thursday and walked them round the whole floor.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: Oh nice, how did that go? I've never actually seen a plant like yours in person.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: You should come. It's loud and a bit hot, but people always find it fascinating once they see the machines running.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: I'd love that, genuinely. Maybe once things calm down a bit I can take a morning and drive out.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Deal. I'll even find you a hard hat that fits, though I can't promise the ear defenders are comfortable.

turns.speaker: Rafiq
turns.text: I'll risk it. Right, I'd better get back to the paper explosion, but I'll let you know the second Marlow surfaces.

turns.speaker: Ottilie
turns.text: Perfect, thanks Rafiq. Talk in a couple of weeks, or sooner if they wake up.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hello Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. Just doing our regular check-in, how are you keeping?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Hello Emeka! Not too bad at all, thanks. A bit tired this week but I think that's just the weather.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Understandable, it's been grey and damp for ages. Have you been getting out for any walks at all?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: A few short ones round the block when it's dry. My granddaughter came over on Saturday and dragged me to the park, so that counted for a good long one.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ha, grandchildren are the best personal trainers. How old is she now?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: She's seven going on seventeen. She wanted to show me how she can do cartwheels, and I told her my cartwheeling days are well behind me.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Quite right too! And how has the eating been lately, in general? Still keeping to regular meals?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Mostly, yes. I'm having more soups and stews this time of year, and I try not to snack in the evenings, though the biscuit tin does call to me now and then.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Soups and stews are a good choice in winter, nice and filling. The odd biscuit isn't the end of the world, just keep an eye on it.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: That's what I tell myself! Oh, by the way, I was filling in a form at my neighbour's and realised I wasn't sure you had it down right. The doctor I'm under is Dr. Grieve.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Thanks for mentioning that, I'll make sure our notes are all in order. Better to double check these things.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Grand. Now, is the flu still going round? Half the women at my church group have been coughing and spluttering.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: It's been a busy season, yes, lots of colds and flu about. Wash your hands well, and if you start feeling feverish or achy, give us a ring early.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I will. I'm keeping my distance from anyone who sounds croaky. My granddaughter had the sniffles last week though, so I'm hoping I escaped.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Fingers crossed. Any other worries you want to raise before I let you go?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: No, I think that's everything. Thanks for ringing, Emeka, it's nice to have someone checking in.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Anytime, Bronagh. I'll be in touch again in a couple of weeks. Mind yourself and stay warm!

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. Got a few minutes for the fortnightly catch-up?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Hi Emeka, yes of course. I'm just having a cuppa so perfect timing.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Lovely. How have you been sleeping these last couple of weeks?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Honestly, not bad. I'm usually out by eleven now, though I still wake up once around four and lie there staring at the ceiling.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's a decent improvement. Four a.m. wake-ups are really common, so try not to stress over it.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I'll try. Oh, and I've been meaning to tell you, I'm on 750 mg of metformin a day now, split with my meals.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Thanks for letting me know, I'll make sure that's noted properly on your record. Any tummy trouble with it?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Nothing to speak of. Also, I started taking omega-3 about a week ago, someone at my book club swore by it.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Good to know, I'll jot that down. How are you finding it so far?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Fine so far, just a bit of a fishy burp now and then. Nothing dramatic.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ha, that's the classic one. Now, next time you come in, how did you find getting a parking space at the clinic?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Ugh, it was a nightmare last time. I circled the car park twice and ended up on the side street.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Mornings are better, before ten it's usually quieter. If you can, book an early slot and you'll walk straight in.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Good tip, I'll ask for the first one of the day.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Are the appointment reminder texts reaching you okay? Some people tell us they arrive too late or not at all.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: They come through fine, usually the day before. Maybe one earlier in the week would help me, but I'm not complaining.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: I'll pass that on to the front desk. Right, I'll let you get back to your tea. Speak in a couple of weeks!

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the surgery. How have you been keeping since we last spoke?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Hi Emeka, not too bad thanks. A bit tired this week but nothing dramatic.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Sorry to hear that. Is the tiredness down to sleep, do you think? How have you been sleeping lately?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Honestly it's been patchy. I drop off fine but I'm awake at 4 most mornings and can't get back down.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's frustrating. Try keeping screens away for the last hour before bed and see if it helps, it works for a lot of people.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I'll give that a go. Oh, before I forget, I'm under Dr. Sato now, I got moved over from my old doctor.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Thanks for letting me know, I'll make sure that's noted on your file. How are you finding the change?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Grand so far, very friendly. And I keep up with my amlodipine every morning, that's just part of the routine now.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Good, sounds like you've got a solid routine. How about the eating side of things, any changes there?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Pretty steady really. I'm trying to have proper meals instead of grazing, and I've cut back on the biscuits with my tea, mostly.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Mostly is a good start! Regular meals tend to make a big difference to how people feel through the day.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: That's what I'm finding. I also started taking vitamin B12 a couple of weeks ago, a friend recommended it for the tiredness.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Okay, good to know. Let's keep an eye on how you feel over the next few weeks and we can talk it through next time.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Sounds good. Has the flu been bad around the surgery? Everyone at my church seems to be coughing.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: It's been a busy season, yes, lots of coughs and colds going round. Wash your hands often and stay away from anyone who's obviously unwell if you can.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Will do. Thanks Emeka, talk in a couple of weeks then.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Absolutely, take care of yourself and try to get some rest, Bronagh.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. How are you getting on this week?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Hello Emeka! Not bad at all, thanks. Bit tired but I can't complain.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Glad to hear it. Has the tiredness been creeping in, or is it just the end of a long week?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Mostly the sleep, to be honest. I've been waking up around four and then lying there staring at the ceiling.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's frustrating. Is it every night, or just now and then?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: More nights than not this past fortnight. Last night was better though, I got a solid stretch until half six.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Well that's a good sign. Try keeping the room a bit cooler and avoid tea late in the evening, sometimes that helps.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I'll swap to decaf after tea time and see. My daughter says I'm on the screen too much at night as well.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: She might have a point there! Has the flu been going around where you are? We've had a lot of people in the surgery with it this winter.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Oh yes, half the street has had it. I had my jab back in the autumn so I seem to have dodged it, touch wood.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Good, that's exactly what we like to hear. It does seem to be easing off now, thankfully.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Not before my grandson caught it, poor lamb. He was off school for a week and sounded dreadful on the phone.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ah, no. Is he back on his feet now?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: He is, and full of beans again. He's been telling me all about a football match he scored in, I had to hear it twice.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Brilliant, that must have cheered you up. Sounds like you're a proud nan.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Very proud! Anyway, I'll try the decaf and the cooler room, and let you know how the sleep goes.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Perfect, do that. I'll check in again in a couple of weeks, take care of yourself Bronagh.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. Just doing your fortnightly check-in, have you got a few minutes?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Hi Emeka, yes, go on. I'm just home from running errands actually.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Lovely. How are you getting on generally this week?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Not bad at all. Bit tired, but nothing out of the ordinary.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Tired in what way? How's the sleep been lately?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Up and down, to be honest. A couple of nights I was wide awake at 3am staring at the ceiling, but the last few have been better.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's good that it's settling. Anything that seems to help when you do get a good night?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Keeping the phone out of the bedroom, mostly. And not having tea too late in the evening.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Sensible. And how about the eating, are you keeping to a fairly steady routine?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Mostly, yes. I'm trying to cook more at home instead of grabbing something on the go, though weekends get a bit loose.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's pretty normal, honestly. Regular meals during the week is the main thing, and a bit of give at the weekend is fine.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Good to hear. Oh, before I forget, parking at the clinic was a nightmare last time I came in. I ended up circling for ages.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ah, yes, it fills up fast in the mornings. Afternoon slots are usually easier, and there's the overflow car park round the back of the building.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I didn't know about the back one. I'll try that next time, thanks.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: No problem. Right, I think that's everything for today. Keep up the good work and I'll check in again in a couple of weeks.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Brilliant, thanks Emeka. Talk to you then.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. How are you getting on this week?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Hi Emeka! Not bad at all, thanks. Feeling a bit more settled than last time we spoke.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Glad to hear it. Did you get a look at your latest blood test result?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I did, the letter came through and my HbA1c was 7.5%. I wasn't sure whether to be pleased or not, to be honest.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's a reasonable place to be, and we can talk it through properly at your next review. How have the meals been going day to day?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Pretty steady. I've been keeping to regular meal times and trying not to snack so much in the evenings, though the weekends are always a bit looser.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's very normal, regular timing helps more than people think. Are you getting out and about much?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Yes, I've been walking a lot more lately. Most mornings I go round the park before the day gets going, and I actually look forward to it now.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's brilliant, keep that up. By the way, I noticed a note on your file about the doctor. Is that still the same one?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Oh, good catch. I'm with Dr. Fontaine now, they moved me over a little while ago and it's been fine so far.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Lovely, I'll make sure that's all up to date on my side. Are you coming into the clinic for anything soon?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Next week I think, yes. Parking there is always a nightmare though, I end up circling the car park for ages.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ha, I know, it fills up fast. If you come a bit before your appointment there's usually a space at the far end by the side road.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Good tip, I'll aim to get there early. Oh, one more thing, I started taking zinc a couple of weeks ago, just on a whim really.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Thanks for telling me, I'll jot that down so we have the full picture. Anything else on your mind before I let you go?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: No, I think that's everything. Thanks for the call, Emeka, talk in a couple of weeks!

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. How's your week going so far?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Hi Emeka! Not bad at all, bit of a grey day here but I can't complain.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Glad to hear it. Did that reminder text come through okay for your next appointment? We've switched the wording on them recently.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: It did, yes. Nice and clear this time, I even got a second nudge the day before which was handy.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Good, that's the idea. Anything you've been meaning to tell me since we last spoke?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Actually yes, I've been moved over to Dr. Hallberg now, so I'll be seeing a different face at the surgery.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Thanks for letting me know, I'll make sure that's reflected on my side. How have you been sleeping lately?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Up and down, to be honest. Some nights I'm out like a light and others I'm staring at the ceiling at 3am.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's frustrating. Is there a pattern, like worse after a busy day or after a late evening?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Probably worse when I've been sitting around all day. Oh, and I go to physio every week now, which tires me out in a good way.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's great to hear, regular movement often helps with sleep too. Keep an eye on whether the good nights line up with the physio days.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I'll do that. I also started taking iron a couple of weeks ago, not sure if that's got anything to do with how I feel.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Worth noting down. Just jot it in your diary alongside how you sleep and we can chat through it next time.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Will do. Is there much of the flu going around at the surgery at the minute?

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: It's quietened down now the season's winding up, but we'll be sending out reminders again in the autumn so keep an eye on your phone.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Perfect, I'll watch for it. Thanks for the call, Emeka, talk in a couple of weeks!

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Take care, Bronagh. Speak soon!

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. How's your week been so far?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Hi Emeka! Not bad at all, a bit busy but good. Glad it's a bank holiday, I needed the lie-in.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ha, same here. Speaking of which, how have you been sleeping lately?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Much better than a few weeks ago, actually. I'm mostly dropping off quickly and only waking once or twice, which is a big improvement.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's great to hear. Good sleep makes everything else easier. Are you getting out and about much?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Yeah, I've been walking more in general. The evenings are lighter so I've been going out after tea most days, even if it's just round the block.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Brilliant, that's the sort of habit that really sticks. And how about the eating side of things?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Pretty steady, I think. I'm cooking at home more and snacking less, though I won't pretend the odd biscuit doesn't sneak in.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Nobody's perfect, and the odd biscuit won't undo the good work. Anything else on your mind health-wise?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Well, I was going through my tablets the other day to tidy the box, and I take atorvastatin in the evening with my tea, so I keep it by the kettle so I don't forget.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Keeping it somewhere you see it every day is a smart trick. Lots of people swear by that.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Oh, and one other thing, I started taking magnesium a little while back. A friend of mine recommended it for sleep, so maybe that's part of why I'm doing better.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Good of you to mention it, I'll make a note on your record. Have you noticed any difference with your tummy or anything else since starting?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: No, nothing odd at all. I just feel a bit more settled in the evenings.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Lovely. Keep up the walking and the good sleep, and I'll check in again in a couple of weeks.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Will do, thanks Emeka. Talk to you then!

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. How are you getting on this week?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Hi Emeka, not bad thanks. Bit tired, the lift at the clinic was out when I came by on Tuesday and I had to do all those stairs.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ah yes, sorry about that. It's been broken for days and the engineer keeps promising he'll be in. If the stairs are a problem, tell reception and we can book you a room on the ground floor.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: That would help, thanks. I'll mention it next time.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: And how's the sleeping going? Last time you said you were waking up a lot.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: A bit better actually. I'm getting maybe six hours straight now, instead of waking at three every night. The heat doesn't help though.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Good, that's progress. Keep the room cool and try to keep a regular bedtime if you can.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Will do. By the way, I was weighed at the last visit and they put it down as 86 kg, if you're updating my notes.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Thanks, I'll make a note of that. Did the text reminder for your next appointment come through okay?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Oh wait, I got that wrong earlier, sorry. It's not 86 kg, that was a mistake on my part. It's 91 kg.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: No problem, thanks for catching it. I'll correct it. And on the reminders, you should get a text a couple of days before and another on the morning.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Yes, both came through last time, they're handy. I just pick up my prescriptions from Linden Chemist on my way home, so I usually see them there.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Lovely. And just so my notes are tidy, your blood pressure tablet is ramipril and it has been all along, so nothing's changed there.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Right. Anyway, the other thing is I've stopped taking the vitamin B12, I just wasn't getting on with it.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Okay, thanks for telling me, I'll jot that down. We can talk it through at your next visit if you like.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Sounds good. Hopefully the lift is fixed by then!

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the surgery. How are you doing this week?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Hi Emeka! Not too bad, thanks. Bit tired but nothing dramatic.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Tired how? Are you sleeping okay at the moment?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Honestly it's been patchy. I'm out like a light by eleven but then I'm awake at four and can't get back off.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That early waking is annoying. Does it happen most nights or just now and then?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Maybe three nights out of seven. The other nights I sleep fine, so I'm not complaining too loudly.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Fair enough. Have you been getting out for walks much? Sometimes a bit of fresh air in the day helps the night side of things.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I have, actually. I've been walking a lot more lately, round the park most mornings if the weather behaves. I feel better for it.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's brilliant to hear. Keep that going. Oh, while I have you, I was looking at your notes and I want to check something. I think I've got the wrong chemist down for you.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Yes, that was my mistake, sorry. It's not Linden Chemist where I collect my prescriptions, it's Harbour Dispensary.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: No bother at all, I'll get that corrected on your record today. Thanks for catching it.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: While we're sorting out the details, I was filling in a form for a first aid course and realised I never told you my blood type. It's B negative.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Good to know, I'll add that in too. Handy to have on file.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Is the flu jab clinic going to be starting soon? I'd rather get it done early this year.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: We usually open bookings in the autumn, so keep an eye out. Flu season can be nasty, so it's sensible to plan ahead.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Will do. Thanks, Emeka, talk in a couple of weeks then!

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. How have you been getting on this week?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Hi Emeka! Not bad at all, thanks. Bit tired but nothing dramatic.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Glad to hear it. How have you been sleeping, are you getting a decent stretch at night?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Mostly yes, though I've been waking around 4am and then lying there thinking about my to-do list. Once I get back off I'm fine.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's pretty common, especially when the nights are so light at this time of year. Try keeping the phone out of the bedroom if you can.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Good shout, I do scroll a bit in bed. I'll leave it downstairs for a few nights and see.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: And how's the eating going? Any weeks where it's felt harder to stay on track?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Pretty steady, I've been doing more cooking from scratch and fewer takeaways. The odd biscuit sneaks in with the tea, but I'm not beating myself up about it.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That sounds like a sensible approach. Small habits like that add up over time.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Oh, before I forget, I got my latest blood test result back and my HbA1c is down to 6.8% now. I was chuffed when I saw it.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's lovely news, well done you. All that steady effort is clearly paying off.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Thanks! By the way, did you ever get the lift at the clinic sorted? It was out of order when I came in last time and I had to take the stairs.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ha, no, it's still broken I'm afraid. Engineers keep promising a fix, so for now it's stairs or the ramp round the side.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Fair enough, it's good exercise anyway. Oh, and one thing worth having noted on my record, I'm allergic to penicillin, in case anything ever comes up.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Thanks for flagging that, it's always worth double-checking. I'll make sure it's clear in your notes.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Brilliant. Same time in a couple of weeks then?

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Sounds good. Take care, and enjoy the sunshine in the meantime!

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hi Bronagh, how's your week been going? Hope you're keeping well.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Not bad at all, thanks Emeka. Bit of a sniffle going round at my sister's place though, so I'm keeping my distance.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Sensible. The flu season seems to be dragging on this year, we've had a steady stream of coughs through the clinic.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I can believe it. Speaking of the clinic, I came in last time and the lift was out of order again. Had to get up the stairs the slow way!

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ah, sorry about that. It's been temperamental for ages and everyone's fed up with it. Hopefully they get an engineer in soon.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: No bother, the stairs did me good. Oh, I meant to tell you, my latest HbA1c came back and it's 7.2%.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's lovely to hear, Bronagh. You've clearly been putting the work in.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I'm chuffed with it. I think the biggest thing has been just paying more attention to what I eat day to day.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That makes a big difference. Are you finding it easy enough to keep up, or does it get tedious?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Mostly easy now, it's become habit. I do slip at weekends, a bit of baking creeps in when the grandchildren visit.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ha, that's totally normal. A little treat now and then is fine, it's the everyday pattern that matters most.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: That's what I tell myself! I've been trying to do more vegetables and fewer biscuits with the tea.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Brilliant, small swaps like that really add up over time. Keep doing what you're doing.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I will. Should I do anything different before we chat again?

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Nothing special, just carry on as you are. I'll check in again in a couple of weeks and we'll see how things look.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Sounds good. Thanks Emeka, and mind yourself with all those coughs going round the clinic!

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. Hope you're having an alright week.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Hi Emeka, yes not bad thanks. Bit of a faff getting parked at the clinic last time though, I was circling for ages.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ah, you're not the first to say that. The car park fills up by mid-morning, so early appointments are your best bet if you can manage one.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Good tip, I'll ask for an early slot next time.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Speaking of the clinic, we're already starting to plan for flu season. Are you thinking of getting your jab this year?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Yes definitely, I always get it. My sister had a horrible bout last winter and it put me right off risking it.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Sensible. It's especially worth it with diabetes, since a bad flu can knock your sugars about. We'll let you know when the clinics open up.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Brilliant. Oh, one thing I meant to mention, I got taken off the atorvastatin a while back.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Thanks for telling me, I'll make sure that's noted properly on your record. How have you been feeling since?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Honestly fine, no complaints at all. Just wanted you to have the right picture.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's really helpful. How about the eating, generally speaking? Any changes lately?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Mostly good. I've been doing more cooking from scratch, lots of veg, though I do slip with biscuits in the afternoon.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ha, the afternoon biscuit is a classic. Maybe try keeping some fruit or a few nuts handy so there's an easy swap when the craving hits.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I might try that. Having them within reach is half the battle.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Exactly. Well, I'll leave you to it, and I'll check in again in a couple of weeks.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Lovely, thanks Emeka. Talk soon!

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. How's your week been so far?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Hi Emeka, not bad at all, thanks. A bit muggy today but I can't complain.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Glad to hear it. Did you manage to get in to the clinic okay last time? I know the car park can be a nightmare.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Oh don't get me started. I circled for ages and ended up on the side street, which was a bit of a trek.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Yes, it's been busy lately. Sorry about that, I hear it from a lot of people.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: And then the lift was out of order, so I had to take the stairs up. Not ideal when you're already puffing from the walk.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ah, the lift again. It's been playing up on and off, and I think someone's meant to come and look at it. Hopefully it's sorted soon, because it's a pain for everyone.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: To be fair, the stairs probably did me good. I've been trying to walk more anyway.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's great to hear. Where do you usually go?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Mostly just round the neighbourhood and sometimes down by the park if the weather's decent. Nothing dramatic, I just try to get out most days.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's the way to do it. Little and often adds up more than people think.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: That's what I tell myself when I'm putting my shoes on and don't fancy it.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ha, we all do that. Once you're out the door it's usually fine.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: It is. Though I might park a bit further out next time and make a proper walk of it, since I'll be doing it anyway.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Not a bad plan. Right, I'll let you get on with your day, and I'll be in touch again in a couple of weeks.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Lovely, thanks Emeka. Talk to you then.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Morning Emeka. Sorry, I was out the back hanging washing when you rang.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: No bother at all, Bronagh. How have you been keeping since we last spoke?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Not bad. Sleep has been a bit better actually, I'm getting through most nights without waking at three like I was.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Glad to hear that. Any idea what's helped?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I think it's just cutting out the tea after dinner. And the evenings are getting cooler so the room isn't stuffy anymore.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That makes sense. A cooler room does make a difference for a lot of people.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: My granddaughter stayed over last weekend and she was up at six bouncing on my bed, so that undid a bit of the good work. Her mornings start early, and with my 500 mg tablet to remember on top of it I was all over the place that morning!

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ha, sounds like a lively visit. How old is she now, five?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Six in October. She's just started in the new class and she's full of stories about her teacher.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Lovely age for that. Is she keeping well, no bugs from school yet?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Not yet, touch wood. Mind you, it's only a matter of time once they're all sharing pencils and coughs.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: True enough. Speaking of which, flu season is coming up, so we'll be sending out the invitations for the jab soon.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Oh good, I always get it done early. I had a rotten dose of it a couple of winters ago and I'm not keen to repeat that.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Sensible. It's worth getting it in before everything starts circulating.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Oh, and I meant to say, I stopped taking the omega-3 a while back. I just wasn't noticing any difference.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Okay, thanks for letting me know. I'll ring again in a couple of weeks, and mind yourself with that little one bouncing about.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. Just checking in like we do. How's your week been?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Hello Emeka! Grand, grand. My granddaughter was round on Saturday and she's learned to ride her bike without the stabilisers, so I've been grinning ever since.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Oh that's lovely! Did you get to watch her go up and down the road?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I did, I stood at the gate like a proud old woman and clapped. She wobbled once and got straight back on, no fuss at all.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Good for her. Kids bounce back so quickly. How have you been sleeping lately, by the way?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Better than I was, actually. I used to wake at three and lie there with my mind racing, but this last while I've been going through till half six most mornings.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: That's great to hear. Is it something you've changed in the evenings, or has it just settled on its own?

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I think it's just settled. I switched the telly off earlier and read a bit instead, which probably helps, though I'd not swear to it.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Well, whatever it is, keep doing it. A quiet routine before bed does make a difference for a lot of people.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I will. Oh, before I forget, I keep getting those text reminders from the surgery about appointments. Are they meant to come twice?

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Ah, yes, the system sends one a few days before and a second the day before. A bit of a nudge so nobody forgets, though I can see how it feels like a lot.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Oh no, I don't mind at all, it's handy. I used to scribble things on the calendar and then forget to look at it, so the text beats me every time.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Brilliant, then it's doing its job. If it ever gets annoying just let us know and we can look at changing it.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: Will do. Anyway, I'd better go, I promised my neighbour a cup of tea and she'll be at the door any minute.

turns.speaker: Emeka
turns.text: Off you go then, enjoy the tea and say hello to the cyclist from me. Talk to you again soon, Bronagh.

turns.speaker: Bronagh
turns.text: I will, thanks Emeka. Mind yourself!

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning Anouk. Did you get a chance to look at the window display yesterday?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: I did, I swapped the old jerseys for the spring ones. It looks a lot brighter from the street now.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Good, it was looking tired. Did anyone stop to look at it?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: A couple of people stood outside for a while. Also I was going over the books last night and remembered the rent is $2,600 a month, so I'm trying to see how many sales we need just to cover that.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Yeah, that's the number that keeps me up. Let's keep pushing the service bookings, those are steady money.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Agreed. A customer asked me about the price on the phone and I wanted to be sure I quoted it right.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: A basic service is $65, so just tell them that. Anything extra we quote after we've had a look at the bike.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Perfect, that's what I said. Are you riding in the local race next weekend, by the way?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: I'm thinking about it, but my legs say no. I haven't been out properly in weeks.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: You should at least come and watch. A few of our regulars are signed up and they'll want to wave at you.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Fair enough, I'll bring a flask and cheer from the side of the road.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Speaking of flasks, the kettle in the back room is making a horrible rattling noise again.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Ha, that thing is ancient. If you're passing a shop this week, grab a cheap new one, and keep the receipt.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Oh, and if anyone asks who to talk to about a tricky repair, send them to Wilhelmina. She's our lead mechanic and she'll sort it out.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Will do. She's been great with the odd wheel jobs lately too.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: She really has. Right, I'll see you Monday, enjoy the rest of your weekend.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning Anouk. Some van is parked right across our door again, I had to squeeze past with the shutter half up.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Ugh, again? I saw it from the corner earlier, the driver was just sitting there on his phone.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: I knocked on his window and he just waved at me. Anyway, he finally moved, so we're open properly now.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Good. Are you in all day or should I plan to open up tomorrow?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: I'm in today, and tomorrow morning too. Oh, before I forget, the red Cube came in on the delivery this morning, it's sitting in the back by the stand.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Nice, I'll go have a look at it after lunch. Does it need anything before we put it on the floor?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Just a wipe down and the tags. I'd say give it a quick check over too, you know how I am about that.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Sure thing. Did you hear about the race on Saturday, the one that goes through the old town and out along the canal?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Yes! A couple of the regulars were talking about it last week. Are you thinking of entering?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Ha, no way, my legs wouldn't survive it. But my cousin is riding it, so I'll probably go stand at the bridge and shout at him.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: That's the right way to do it. Bring a flask, it was freezing out there last time.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Noted. By the way, the workshop is a bit of a state, there's grease all over the bench and the floor by the stand is sticky.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Yeah, I know, I've been ignoring it. Could we do a proper clean on Thursday afternoon when it's quiet?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Thursday works. I'll bring my own gloves this time, the ones in the drawer are all stiff.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Good plan. I'll pick up some degreaser on my way in, the bottle we have is nearly empty.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Perfect. See you in a bit then, I'm just locking up my bike outside.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Morning! Heads up, there's a delivery van parked right across our door again. The driver says he'll be ten minutes, which I don't believe.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Ha, classic. Go out and give him your best polite stare, that usually works.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Already did. He's moving it now, grumbling a bit.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Good. Anything interesting from the weekend rush?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Quite a few people asking about tune-ups. I've been telling them a basic service is $49 now, and nobody's flinched so far.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Great, that's what I hoped to hear. People are usually fine with it if you're upfront.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Also, the punctures! Ever since the roadworks on the main road started I've fixed about a puncture a day. Little bits of grit and metal everywhere.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: I figured. I rode through there last week and could hear the crunching. We should put up a little sign warning people to take the side street.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Good idea, I'll scribble one on the whiteboard by the counter.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Oh, before I forget, the delivery that came in Friday had something fun in it. A new one arrived in stock: the Cannondale Tesoro.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Oh nice, I saw the box but didn't want to open it without you. Should I build it up and put it near the window?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Yes please, front and center. Might catch some eyes from the street.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Will do. Oh, and did you hear about the charity ride next month? A couple of customers asked if we'd be doing a tune-up table at the start.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Sure, count me in. I love those events, it's the sort of thing that makes me glad we've kept this place going since we first opened in 2011.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Ha, that's a long time. I'll put together a sign-up sheet for helpers, then.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Perfect. Thanks Anouk, talk soon!

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning Anouk! Did you see the road race went right past the end of our street last weekend? Half the neighbourhood was out with cowbells.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: I did, I caught the tail end on my way in. Looked like a great turnout this year.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Got the new lease paperwork back, by the way. The rent is $2,350 a month now, so I'll need to watch the budget a bit closer.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Ouch, okay. Well, let me know if there's anything I can do to help on the sales side.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Will do. That man with the creaky crankset came back yesterday, by the way. Third time this month, and he still insists it's our fault.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Oh no, the one who wanted a refund on a tune-up from last year? He cornered me last time for twenty minutes.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: That's the one. Anyway, I've set a basic service at $55 from now on, so update the little sign by the counter when you get a minute.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Sure, I'll redo the sign this afternoon.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Also, online orders are all going out with Dropswift these days, so use their labels when you pack the boxes.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Sorry, I got that wrong, it's not Dropswift at all. We ship with Parcelwing, so grab the labels from that drawer.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Got it, Parcelwing. Good thing you caught that before I printed anything.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Do you want me to change the window display this week? The spring flowers have gotten a bit sad and dusty.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Yes please, something brighter. Maybe pull the yellow bike forward and hang a few helmets from the ceiling.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Love that. I'll string up some of the old race bunting too, it'll look cheerful.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Oh, and a new e-bike showed up in stock this morning, the Specialized Como. Put it near the front once the display is done.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Nice, I'll give it the spot right by the door. Does it need anything before it goes on the floor?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Just a quick wipe down and a tyre check. By the way, I ran into our landlord, Mrs. Pemberton, at the bakery, and she says hello to you.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Aw, that's sweet. Tell her hi back next time. I'm heading to the back to start on the window now.
