turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning Anouk. Did you see the road race going through town on Saturday? Half the high street was lined with people.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: I did, I watched the finish from outside the bakery. The sprint was tight, the winner barely got his wheel over the line first.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Nice. I was hoping a few of them might pop in for spares afterwards, but nobody did.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Ha, they all had their own mechanics with vans. Still, a few spectators asked me where to get a decent helmet.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Good, point them our way next time. Anything else happening in the shop this week?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Mostly punctures. Ever since they finished the roadworks on the bridge road, people keep coming in with flats.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Yeah, I figured. There's probably gravel and bits of metal left in the gutters after the digging.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: That's what I told one customer. He'd had three flats in a week and thought he'd just been unlucky.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Maybe we should stick a note on the door warning people to ride away from the kerb there.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Good idea, I'll write one up this afternoon. Might even sell a few puncture-resistant tyres off the back of it.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Cunning. Right, small favour, can you check the kettle in the back? It was making a weird clicking noise on Friday.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: I noticed that too. It takes ages to boil now and the lid doesn't sit right either.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Sounds like it's on its way out. Descale it first, and if that doesn't help we'll just get a new one.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Will do. I'll try the vinegar trick before we spend anything.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Perfect. A shop without tea is a sad shop.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Agreed. I'll let you know how the kettle goes, and I'll get that door note done too.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning Anouk. Rough start here, the kettle in the back has finally given up. Just clicks and does nothing.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Oh no, that thing has been wheezing for months. I can bring my old one from home tomorrow if you like?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Yes please, you're a lifesaver. I can't function on instant coffee from the café down the road.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Deal. How was the afternoon yesterday? I left right after the man with the wobbly wheel came in.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Ha, he was the easy one. Right after you left, the woman who returned her helmet came back and argued for twenty minutes that we'd scratched it. It had a scratch in the photo on her own phone from before she bought it.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Oof. Did she leave happy at least?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Not exactly, but she left. I kept smiling and said very little, which I'm told is the trick.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Textbook. Honestly I think half of them just want someone to listen.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: True. Oh, before I forget, the Orbea Vibe came in this morning, so there's a new box in the back room. I'd like it out on the shop floor by Friday.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Nice, I'll clear a spot near the window tomorrow and wipe it down once it's built.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Perfect. Also, have you noticed how many people are coming in with punctures since they dug up the road by the bridge?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Yes! Three on Monday alone, and two of them said it was the gravel they'd been riding through where the roadworks are.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Makes sense. Debris everywhere along that stretch. I might put a little note by the counter telling people to check their tyres for embedded bits.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Good idea, I can write it up on the chalkboard. People actually read that.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Brilliant, thanks. And don't forget the kettle tomorrow, I mean it!

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Ha, written on my hand already. See you in the morning.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning Anouk. How's the shop looking? I'm stuck at the dentist till eleven.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Morning! Quiet so far, but I've already fixed three punctures since opening. Ever since they dug up the road by the station, people keep riding through the gravel.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Ha, the roadworks are good for business at least. Any pattern to the punctures?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Mostly thorns and little bits of metal in the tyres. I've started handing out a leaflet on checking tyres after rides, people seem to appreciate it.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Nice touch. Did that guy with the cracked saddle ever come back?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Oh, him. Yes, yesterday, and he insisted it was a manufacturing fault even though he'd clearly dropped the bike. I stayed polite and offered to order him a new saddle, but he left grumbling.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Classic. You handled it better than I would have. I'd have raised my eyebrows and said something sarcastic.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: That's why I'm on the counter and you're doing the paperwork 😄 By the way, I looked at the letter that came in the post for you. The monthly rent has changed and is now $2,100, so you'll want to update the budget sheet.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Ah, thanks for flagging that. I'll sort the spreadsheet tonight.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: No rush. I also redid the window display this week, by the way. I moved the helmets to the left and put a row of bells and lights along the bottom.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: I walked past on Tuesday and it looked great. Much brighter than before. Did the new poster go up too?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Yes, the spring one with the green banner. A couple of people stopped to take photos of it, which felt like a win.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Good. Oh, and one thing I forgot to tell you: the Orbea Vibe was sold on Monday, so you can take it off the floor list and free up that spot.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Oh nice, I'll move something else into that gap right away. Maybe the red commuter bike so it catches the eye from the window.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Perfect idea. Right, they're calling me in. Text you after?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Sure, good luck at the dentist! I'll keep the puncture tally going for you.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning Anouk. Rough start here, a guy came in at opening and spent twenty minutes telling me his bike was 'obviously defective' when the chain was just bone dry.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Oh no, I hope you didn't take it personally. Did he at least buy some lube?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: He did, after a lot of sighing. Anyway, quick thing for your shift tomorrow, the till software we use is Cashwise, so the login on the front counter is the one you want.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Okay, I'll sign in with that one then.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Wait, no, scratch that, I got it wrong. It's not Cashwise, that was a mistake on my part. The till runs ShopKeep One.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Ha, good thing you caught that before I went hunting for the wrong icon. ShopKeep One, got it.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Yeah, my brain is somewhere else today. I've been thinking about redoing the window display, it's looked the same since April.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: I'd love that. The faded poster in the corner is looking pretty sad now. Maybe something with summer touring gear?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Good idea. Panniers, a couple of frame bags, maybe that old steel touring frame hanging up high.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Perfect. Are you going to the club race on Saturday, by the way? The one on the loop by the reservoir?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Thinking about it, yes. I'll bring the repair stand and the pump so we can help out riders at the start line.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Nice, that gets our name out there. A few people asked me last week if we'd be around.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Good. Oh, and before I forget, we're open on Sundays now, so put your name down if you want any of those shifts.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Oh, I'll take a look at the rota tonight. Could be nice to pick up some extra hours.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Great. Also, the Cannondale Tesoro was sold yesterday afternoon, so you can take it off the used rack and tidy that spot up.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Nice, that one had been sitting there forever! I'll clear the space and maybe use it for the display bits.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Perfect, thanks Anouk. See you tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning Anouk. How was the weekend crowd? I got your message about the guy with the wheel.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Oh, don't remind me. He came back twice on Saturday insisting we'd 'ruined' his rear wheel, when it was already out of true when he walked in.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Ha, I know the type. Did you manage to calm him down in the end?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Eventually. I showed him the photo we took when he dropped it off and he went quiet and just muttered something about 'checking with his brother'.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Good thinking with the photo. Keep doing that for any wheel that looks dodgy.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Will do. Also, have you noticed how many punctures we've been fixing since they finished the roadworks on the main road?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Yes! I figured it was just me. Bits of gravel and little metal shavings everywhere, I assume.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Exactly. I pulled a tiny sliver of metal out of a tyre this morning that was practically invisible. People keep coming in thinking they've been unlucky.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Maybe we put a little note by the till telling people to check their tyres after riding through there. Might save them a trip.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Funny, that would actually cost us business, but I like it. Honest advice gets people coming back anyway.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: That's the idea. Oh, and was it the same van again blocking the door on Friday?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Yes, parked right across the entrance for like twenty minutes. A lady with a pushchair couldn't get in and I had to go out and ask the driver to move.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Unbelievable. Was he at least apologetic?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: He shrugged and said he was 'just two minutes'. I wanted to say something but I just smiled and held the door.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: You were more polite than I would've been. If it happens again, take a photo of the plate and I'll ring the depot.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Perfect, I'll do that. Right, I'm going to go sweep up the front before it gets busy.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning Anouk. Did you survive Saturday on your own? I heard it got a bit busy after lunch.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Barely! We had that man back again who wants his money back on the helmet he's clearly worn for months. I stayed polite but it took forever.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Ugh, the one with the red face and the receipt he can never find? Please don't give in, we've been over this with him twice.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: I didn't. I offered to look at the strap since it seemed loose, and he stormed off muttering. Honestly a relief.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Good. Don't lose sleep over him. Did you get a chance to do anything with the window?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Yes, I swapped everything over on Friday evening. Put the old steel frame on the left with the bunting around it, and a little row of bells on the sill.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Sounds lovely. I'll walk past later and have a look from across the street. Does the bunting stay up in the sun or is it fading?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: It's fading a bit on the side that gets the afternoon light. I might flip it around in a couple of weeks so it wears evenly.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Smart. Oh, and how are the punctures looking? Since they finished the roadworks on the main road I keep hearing people complain.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Still coming in, a few every day. It's mostly little bits of gravel and sharp stone chips they left along the edge where the cyclists ride.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: That's what I figured. Maybe we should put a note on the counter reminding people to check their tyres for embedded bits before they ride off again.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Good idea, I'll write one up. People do seem to appreciate when we tell them what caused it rather than just patching and sending them out.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Exactly, it saves them coming back annoyed. Thanks for handling the awkward customer, by the way.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: No problem. I'll do the note this afternoon and take a photo of the window for you too.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Perfect. Send it over when you have a minute, and have a good rest of the weekend.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning Anouk. Did you remember to fill the kettle before you left yesterday? I came in and it was bone dry and stone cold.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Oops, that was me, sorry. I got distracted by the phone and just bolted out the door.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: No harm done, I just had to wait ages for my tea. Anyway, I got the letter about the shop's rent, it's now $1,950 a month. Not the best news for a Sunday.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Ugh, that's a jump. Well, at least we're busy enough to cover it.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: True, and busy is the word. How many punctures came in this week?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Loads. Ever since the roadworks on the high street started, people keep riding through all that grit and gravel. I fixed about four just yesterday afternoon.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Typical. The council tears the road up and we get the tire trouble. Maybe we should put a sign in the window about it.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Ha, a sign saying 'blame the council' would probably go down well with the regulars.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Right, we're getting a new box of tubes in, by the way. Our inner-tube supplier is Spindle & Co, so it should be the usual stuff.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Good, we were running low on the narrow ones. Oh, and did you hear about that guy on Thursday?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: The one who wanted a refund on a helmet he'd clearly dropped off a roof? I was in the back, so I only caught the shouting.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: That's him. He kept insisting it came out of the box cracked, and then he asked to speak to the manager three times.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Sounds exhausting. Did you manage to calm him down in the end?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Sort of. I offered him a discount on a new one and he went away muttering, but at least he went.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Good call. Oh, before I forget, a couple of tourists asked me yesterday if we do rentals, and yes, the shop offers bike rentals, so point them to me next time.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Will do. I'll put the kettle on now, since you're clearly in need of a decent cup of tea.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning Anouk. Ugh, a delivery van has been parked right in front of the door for twenty minutes, nobody can even get in.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Oh no, I'm just around the corner. Want me to knock on the driver's window when I get there?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Please do. Honestly I think he's having a coffee somewhere. Anyway, I'm planning to clean the workshop properly this week, Saoirse is already moaning about the grease on the floor by the stand.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Ha, fair enough, it's been bad since the spring. I can do the floor and the shelves if you take care of the tool wall?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Deal. I'll sort the tools Wednesday. Also we haven't opened on Sundays since last month, so at least there's a quiet day to get this kind of stuff done.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Yeah, I noticed it's been much calmer. I actually got to see my family last weekend for once.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Good, that was the whole idea. Oh, and the van just left, so you can walk in like a normal person now.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Perfect timing, I'm two minutes away. Should I do the window display today too? It still has that faded summer poster.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Yes please. The sun has bleached everything in there anyway. I'd like something that looks fresh, maybe more autumn colours.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Okay, I'll dig out the orange banner from the storeroom. Do you want the helmets in the window or just the bikes?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Mostly bikes, plus a couple of helmets on stands. And the Ribble Hybrid arrived in stock on Friday, so put that one front and centre.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Nice, I saw the box in the back. I'll unwrap it and wipe it down before it goes in the window.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Great. Don't leave fingerprints on the frame, it's a pain to get off.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Gloves on, promise. I'll send you a photo of the display when it's done.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Perfect, thanks Anouk. I'll bring pastries tomorrow as payment for the floor scrubbing.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Now you're talking. See you shortly!

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning. Did you see the van outside? Some delivery guy has been parked right across the door for twenty minutes.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Yes, I had to squeeze past with my bag. I knocked on his window and he just waved at me like it was nothing.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Classic. Is he still there? I might go out and have a word.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: He's gone now. Left a parcel on the step though, no ring, no nothing.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Fine, I'll bring it in. How's the morning looking otherwise?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Busy with punctures, honestly. Three already since opening, all people who came through the roadworks on the main road.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Of course they did. All that loose gravel and broken glass they left behind.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: One lady had a sliver of glass right through the tyre. I showed her where it went in and she looked horrified.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Maybe we should put a little note by the till about riding around that stretch. People would appreciate the warning.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Good idea, I'll scribble something on the whiteboard after lunch. Oh, and the kettle is making that rattling noise again.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Ugh, is it still working at least? I can't function without my second tea.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: It works, it just sounds like it's about to take off. The lid also doesn't close properly anymore.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: I'll pick up a new one on my way in tomorrow. Nothing fancy, just something that doesn't scream at us.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Perfect. Maybe get one that's not bright orange this time, it clashes with everything.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Ha, noted. Plain grey it is. Go and rescue that next puncture before the queue gets long.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: On it. Bringing the parcel in first before somebody trips over it.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning Anouk. Did you see the van outside again? Parked right across the door for twenty minutes before I could even get the shutter up.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Ugh, yes, I had to squeeze past it with my bike this morning. The driver just shrugged at me like it was nothing.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Maybe I should put a cone out front or something. A little sign saying loading only for five minutes.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: A cone wouldn't hurt. Or you could just stand in the doorway looking grumpy, that usually works on you anyway.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Ha, thanks. By the way, the kettle is making that clicking noise again. Do you think it's dying?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: It's the limescale, I think. I'll run vinegar through it this afternoon and see if it settles down.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Perfect. I'm not ready to go without tea during the busy hours, I'd be useless.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Agreed, nobody wants to see that. Oh, are you still planning to ride in the charity thing next weekend?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: That's the plan. I haven't trained nearly enough, though. My legs are going to hate me by the halfway point.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: You'll be fine, it's a gentle route along the river. And there are cake stops, I checked.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Cake stops, now you're talking. That changes everything. Are you coming along or just handing out water?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: I'll ride the first half with you and then peel off. My knee is still a bit grumpy after last month.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Fair enough. I'll bring a spare tube and a pump in case anyone needs help along the way.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Good thinking, someone always gets a puncture at those. I'll bring a flask so we don't depend on the kettle.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Ha, very funny. Right, I'm going to go shoo that van if it's still there. Back in a minute.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Good luck, and be polite! I'll sort out the vinegar for the kettle while you're gone.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning Anouk. Did you see the van parked right across our door again? Had to squeeze past with that wheel set.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Ha, yes, I saw it when I got in. The driver was inside someone's flat with a sofa, apparently. Took him twenty minutes to come back.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Classic. Maybe we need a little cone out front that says bikes only.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: I'd buy that cone. Or just a very loud bell by the door.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Are you still riding in the charity ride this weekend?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Yep, signed up weeks ago. It's the flat loop along the river, so nothing scary. I'm mostly going for the cake at the rest stop.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Smart. I'll come by the start and hand out some water bottles if you want a shop banner up too.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Yes please, bring the banner. Oh, and while I think of it, I was doing the stock sheet and our inner tubes come from Northgate Components, same as always.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Good idea on the banner then. I'll stick it on the fence by the registration table.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Perfect. Are you going to watch the local race on Saturday afternoon too?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Maybe for the finish. Half the club will be there, and they always want to chat about their drivetrains afterwards.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: True, we'll probably get a few repair bookings out of it. People get inspired after watching someone sprint.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Ha, fair. Bring a thermos though, it's supposed to be chilly by the course.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Will do. I'll lock up tonight and see you tomorrow, hopefully with the door clear this time.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Fingers crossed. Thanks Anouk, good work today.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Morning Anouk. Did you see the queue of punctures sitting by the back wall? Feels like everyone rode through the roadworks on Hallam Street this week.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: I saw. Half of them are the same story, gravel and bits of glass from the dug-up stretch. I've patched about eight since Wednesday.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Ha, we should send the council a thank-you card. Anyone come in complaining about it?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: One guy yesterday, yes. Insisted the puncture was our fault because he'd bought the tyres here last spring. Not sure how that works.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Oh no. Did he calm down at all?

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Eventually. He kept saying he wanted it done 'properly this time' and then sighed every time I picked up a tool. I just kept smiling and worked faster.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: That's the only way with those. Smile and carry on. I had a woman last week who wanted a discount for waiting ten minutes. In a shop with a sign saying we're busy on Saturdays.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Classic. Did you give her one?

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Offered her a coffee instead. She took it and left happy, so I call that a win.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Smart. Oh, and heads up, the delivery van was parked right across our door again this morning. I had to squeeze past the driver with a wheel in each hand.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Again? That's the third time. I'll have a word next time I see him, politely.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Please do. Customers were literally turning around because they thought we were shut.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: That's the worst part. Lost sales because of a white van. Maybe I'll put a little sign on the pavement saying we're open, just behind it.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Good idea. I can chalk something on the board, a little arrow and a cartoon bike or something.

turns.speaker: Casimir
turns.text: Perfect. Make the bike look annoyed at the van.

turns.speaker: Anouk
turns.text: Will do. I'll finish the last of these punctures first and then get chalking.
